title: Accounts, login and environment selection
fixture: L_FrontEnd / service fixture Account_A and Account_B
purpose: The player selects Development or the configured production realm, authenticates, then receives a character list belonging to that verified account. Login establishes identity, not permission to invent inventory or spawn a pawn.
fields: EnvironmentId: stable allowlisted ID; never an arbitrary client-provided backend URL
AccountId: backend UUID mapped from provider subject; read only on client
AccessToken: transient memory only; never a log, SaveGame or content asset
TokenExpiryUtc: provider/server timestamp; refresh through provider flow
BuildProtocolVersion and ContentCatalogHash: exact server compatibility checks
commands: BeginLogin(EnvironmentId, ProviderChoice) -> Pending|EnvironmentUnavailable; client adapter, asynchronous
SignOut() -> Cleared; local credentials discarded and server session release requested
flow: Choose DA_Environment_Development from a fixed menu; disable any public-connect option in development-auth mode.
URPGAccountSession obtains a provider proof or loopback-only fixture token; the backend validates issuer, audience, expiry and nonce and maps the subject to AccountId.
Backend returns a short-lived app session and immutable character summaries; it does not accept an AccountId supplied as authority by the UI.
WBP_Login leaves Authenticating only on the matching request generation; responses from a previously selected environment are ignored.
WBP_CharacterSelect receives the new list and version. A server admission ticket is requested only after the player selects an owned character.
On expiry, clear or refresh the app session and reconnect from durable state; never reuse an old zone session epoch.
editor_steps: Create L_FrontEnd as an empty level with BP_MenuGameMode and no gameplay pawn. Put a neutral 3D preview floor and preview camera in a separate preview actor.
Create DA_Environment_Development with an allowlisted loopback API origin, display text key and ProtocolVersion=1. Keep credentials out of it.
In BP_RPGPlayerController, create WBP_MainMenu for local controllers only; Login opens WBP_Login, passing the single process-local URPGAccountSession adapter.
Bind LoginButton.OnClicked to BeginLogin and disable the button until that request settles. Bind cancel to a generation increment rather than trying to undo a completed backend login.
Use two fixture identities on a private development network. Production startup must refuse the fixture authenticator even when a client passes its option.
failures: Expired proof -> Unauthorized; remain SignedOut, with no character summaries leaked.
Switch environment while request is outstanding -> old reply ignored; no mixed realm characters.
Select another account's CharacterId -> Forbidden; no zone reservation.
Backend unavailable -> EnvironmentUnavailable; retry has no inventory/character writes.
tuning: Proposed app-token lifetime 15 minutes and explicit refresh; provider limits take precedence. No real password store is implemented by this documentation.
observability: Log correlation ID, environment, provider result code and latency, never credentials or raw identity proofs. Screen reader status text announces pending, failed and signed-in states.

title: Character slots, creation, selection and recovery
purpose: Create a common-body avatar with approved hair/palette/outfit choices and one of Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist or Warden. Class selection changes authored starting rules, not an invented race silhouette. The backend commits name, slot and appearance together.
fields: CharacterId: generated UUID, never derived from name
SlotIndex: integer 0..3 initially; unique per account among nonpurged characters
NormalizedName: server-normalized Unicode key; unique under published realm policy
AppearanceVersion: positive integer plus BodyId, HairId, PaletteId, OutfitPresetId
ClassDefinitionId: one of class.vanguard, class.ranger, class.arcanist, class.warden
DeletionState: Active|SoftDeleted|Purged; deletion timestamps are backend controlled
flow: Appearance controls modify only the preview actor. Validate that each selection exists in the client catalog but repeat validation in the backend.
After confirmation, send the command ID, chosen slot and catalog identifiers; generate no authoritative character UUID in UMG.

Backend authenticates AccountId, checks slot/name uniqueness, class availability and appearance allowlists, and inserts character, starting progression, appearance and command receipt in one transaction.
Starter item grants, when enabled in Phase 09, use a unique character-creation entitlement rather than rerunning grants on every login.
Refresh the slot list from the committed summary and resolve preview visuals with the same appearance resolver used by remote avatars.
After disconnect, list/select the existing CharacterId; target zone loads the durable appearance and replicates only safe appearance IDs.
editor_steps: Create four DA_Class_* definitions with display text, common BodyId=body.common and separate class IDs; abilities can be unassigned until the combat phases.
Place Preview_Avatar in L_FrontEnd with collision disabled, no replication, no PlayerState and no authoritative component; use the art resolver in preview mode.

Build WBP_CharacterCreate with a step heading, previous/next controls, class description, name field and preview rotation disabled. Facing preview buttons are discrete direction choices, not a world camera rotation option.
In WBP_CharacterSelect bind Create, EnterWorld, Delete and Restore to URPGCharacterRoster requests. Delete requires typing the displayed character name and explains the recovery policy.
Reopen BP_RPGPlayerController: after admission completes, remove preview widgets, clear pending input and request the initial zone connection; do not manually spawn an extra gameplay character.
failures: Two simultaneous identical normalized names -> one Created, one NameUnavailable.
Same CommandId with same payload -> same CharacterId; different payload -> IdempotencyConflict.
Hair from unsupported page/body -> InvalidAppearance or a documented cosmetic fallback; no fabricated compatible art.
Delete while character lease is active -> Busy; never remove inventory rows underneath a live session.
Restore name now occupied -> NameConflict and a rename flow; no takeover of another character's name.
tuning: Four slots and a 7-day soft-delete recovery window are proposals. Production naming, moderation, privacy and purge policy require explicit review; no paid character slots.
observability: Audit character create/delete/restore and name-policy reason codes. Do not publish account identity in nameplates. Keyboard/controller focus follows the wizard step heading.

title: Layered sprites, facing, appearance and remote avatars
purpose: Render one 2D body and compatible clothing/weapon layers while a full-height capsule moves on a 3D floor. Presentation selects poses from server-observed action facts; it cannot decide hits, gathering rewards or whether movement is legal.
fields: PresentationState: ActionTag, Facing4, ActionSequenceId, AcceptedStartServerSeconds and variant; replicated compactly
AppearanceIds: body/hair/palette/outfit/gear visual IDs; persist IDs, not component pointers
AnimationKey: body compatibility version + page + action + facing + variant
LayerBindings: body, behind, outfit, cloak, face, hair, hat, main tool, offhand, special overlay; only instantiate supported layers
FootPivotPixels: source-verified coordinates; currently unknown until the archive is inspected
VisualScale: one shared pixels-per-unit choice; do not stretch each wearable separately
commands: ApplyAppearanceSnapshot(AppearanceIds, Revision) -> Applied|MissingVisual; project custom client function
ResolveAnimation(ActionTag, Facing4, EquipmentVisualIds) -> MatchedSet|Fallback; project custom pure lookup
ApplyPresentationState(State) -> Updated|StaleSequence; project custom presentation command
ClearVisualBindings() -> Cleared; unsubscribe and release soft references on teardown
flow: Owning movement/combat/gather components publish a semantic action and accepted timestamp; the server does not send each PNG frame.
URPGPaperDollComponent resolves matching body and gear pages before starting playback. Missing gear may hide that layer but cannot alter equipped stats.
A single PaperZD animation driver selects the body sequence. The project adapter reads its effective frame/normalized time and drives compatible overlays from that same clock.
Facing is derived from movement or action aim in the camera-ground basis with hysteresis; use a four-direction lookup, not diagonal art invented by mirroring.
Remote clients use replicated action sequence/timestamp plus interpolated movement. Late packets skip to the current pose or finish harmlessly; they do not replay gameplay.
On a camera elevation/floor change, keep the capsule and foot anchor in world space. Nameplates and portraits use safe identity/appearance snapshots, never account IDs.
editor_steps: In L_ArtLab place a flat floor, ramp, stair, raised bridge, low wall and overlapping avatar pair; label near/far paths so occlusion errors are observable.

Create ARPGPlayerCharacter from ACharacter and BP_PlayerCharacter as its child after native compilation. Add one noncolliding Paper2D body FlipbookComponent under VisualRoot; keep Capsule and CharacterMovement as collision/movement owners.

Add the project PaperZD adapter and URPGPaperDollComponent. Inspect installed PaperZD source to bind its Animation Component/render component; exact plugin property names are not verified here. Do not add a skeletal montage requirement.
Author DA_AnimationSet_Common mappings only for source-verified sheet/action/facing combinations. Until audit, use developer-created debug pose assets with an obvious development label.
Give all layers identical canvas/pivot/scale. Test masked and translucent materials separately; small ordered layer offsets must not let a cloak sort in front of an unrelated nearer actor.
Reopen BP_PlayerCharacter after each new action phase to add only that action's mapping; reopen WBP_Portrait to use the same IDs and fallback logic.
failures: Outfit page p1 assigned during a pBOW action -> PageMismatch warning and explicit fallback; no shifted limbs.
Body clip missing -> MissingBody diagnostic silhouette; gameplay remains functional in a development lab.
Missing animation notify -> accepted hit/reward and action completion still occur from the authority.
Duplicate action sequence -> no duplicate sound or visual spawn; stale appearance revision ignored.
Two avatars cross a bridge at different heights -> world occlusion and foot alignment remain plausible; record failing material/projection combinations.
tuning: Four facings first. Proposed hysteresis 8° around facing boundaries; shared visual playback timing comes from the actual source guide when available. Eight-direction, swim, cast, dodge and mounted art remain unverified.
observability: Diagnostics show resolved action/page/facing/body/layers and fallback reason. Emote captions and telegraphs never rely only on color. Pixel art imports and legal restrictions are detailed in the art chapters.

title: Capsule locomotion, sprint, jump, dodge and fall damage
purpose: Move freely on the X/Y ground plane, using Z for elevation. CharacterMovement remains the sole movement integrator. Sprint, jump and dodge consume approved intent/resources; art can have only four directions while collision remains fully three-dimensional.
fields: WalkSpeedCmPerSecond=450; SprintSpeed=650; server-owned tunables
CapsuleRadiusCm=34 and HalfHeightCm=88; full-height collision, tune to world
JumpZVelocityCmPerSecond=420; air control is data-defined
DodgeDistanceCm=300; DurationSeconds=0.25; RecoverySeconds=0.35
SprintStaminaPerSecond=8 and DodgeStaminaCost=15; GAS resource owner after Phase 07
SafeFallHeightCm=300; damage curve keyed by server-measured fall distance
SavedMoveIntent: sprint/dodge flags and validated sequence; transient network movement data
commands: SetMoveIntent(Axis2D) -> Cached; local input, normalized magnitude <=1
RequestSprint(bool) -> Predicted|Rejected; movement intent validated on server
RequestJump() and ReleaseJump() -> native Character jump path; no duplicate impulse
flow: Convert Axis2D into a fixed camera-ground forward/right basis. Normalize diagonal keyboard input without discarding analog magnitude.
Feed AddMovementInput into CharacterMovement, not repeated SetActorLocation or a parallel Blueprint movement Tick.

Extend saved-move prediction for sprint/dodge intent so a delayed reliable RPC cannot make speed state diverge from the move being simulated. This is a native implementation task requiring installed CMC API inspection.
Server validates current movement mode, action permissions, stamina and displacement, then simulates the approved movement with capsule sweeps.
Publish movement mode/velocity and accepted dodge sequence to presentation; no sprite notify changes location or restores a dodge budget.
On landing, server computes the fall event once from its own grounded/falling history. GAS applies configured damage after Phase 07; Phase 02 logs the proposed event only.
editor_steps: In BP_PlayerCharacter disable plane constraint and yaw rotation driven by sprite facing. Retain capsule collision against WorldStatic/WorldDynamic as appropriate; sprite components have NoCollision.

Set camera-relative input as Axis2D in IA_Move and map W/S to forward/back and A/D to right/left with the appropriate negate/swizzle modifiers. Confirm values in the input debugger rather than assuming template axis conventions.

Create URPGCharacterMovementComponent as the native movement replacement at character construction; do not add a second movement component in Blueprint. Header/signature edits require a full Editor-closed compile.
Set MaxStepHeight=35 cm and WalkableFloorAngle=40° initially. In L_TerrainLab author stairs at 20/35/45 cm and slopes at 15/30/45° to establish pass/fail boundaries.

Bind Jump Started to the one native Jump route and release/cancel to StopJumping. Bind sprint and dodge to intent APIs; remove legacy coyote/buffer/second-jump platformer paths unless separately designed.
Reopen the movement extension in Phase 07 to replace temporary stamina fixture values with the PlayerState ASC; replay movement tests after that dependency change.
failures: Diagonal full keyboard input -> same top speed as straight input, not sqrt(2) faster.
Dodge into a wall or bridge rail -> capsule stops/slides under collision; no teleport through it.
Sprint packet arrives late -> saved move/prediction corrects state; no permanent speed increase.
Jump repeated in air -> rejected under one-jump policy; changing sprite direction adds no jump.
Death/travel while key held -> input cleared, dodge canceled, no stale action replay after respawn.
Fall below kill floor -> one death/recovery event, never an inventory rollback.
tuning: All listed speeds, capsule dimensions, slopes, stamina and timings are tuning proposals. Start with native jump behavior; do not recreate platformer coyote time or climbing. No climb action is bound.
observability: Record authoritative position/mode, correction distance, action sequence and rejection reason. Test at 30/60/120 fps and 0/80/160 ms latency profiles after Phase 03; those are recipes, not measured results.

title: Water, swimming and shoreline transitions
purpose: Water is a 3D volume with a water surface and reachable shoreline, not a sprite animation state. The player can swim without climbing; fishing access and swimming permissions use related water metadata but different action rules.
fields: WaterBodyId: authored stable ID shared with fishing volumes
SurfaceZCm and bottom/collision geometry: authoring data
SwimSpeedCmPerSecond=250; ExitSlopeDegrees<=35 initially
SubmersionThreshold: capsule water-volume condition, not sprite alpha
CanFishWhileSwimming=false initially; underwater combat disabled initially
DrowningEnabled=false initially; no oxygen UI until a deliberate survival rule exists
commands: EvaluateWaterContact(WaterBodyId, CapsuleState) -> Wading|Swimming|Dry; authoritative movement integration
CancelWaterIncompatibleActions(Reason) -> Canceled; combat/gather/fishing owners handle their own cleanup
flow: Capsule enters a water Physics Volume with water behavior configured; the movement component recognizes Swimming when the actual body conditions are satisfied.
Server chooses movement mode from collision/volume state, never a client-sent IsSwimming truth.
Input applies swimming movement while camera/feet rendering changes cosmetically; temporary art fallback is a labeled common-body pose with a waterline effect.
At shore, collision sweep and walkable-floor result establish grounded movement; do not teleport to a client-selected bank.
Cancel mining, woodcutting and shore-only fishing when authoritative water state invalidates them.
Replicate mode and relevant volume identity; on transfer/reconnect load safe supported spawn coordinates, never inside an unloaded water body.
editor_steps: Create a shallow basin, deep volume and two shoreline ramps in L_TerrainLab. The simple prototype can use a configured Physics Volume; a full Water rendering plugin is not a gameplay requirement.
Set water-volume physics flags in the installed Editor and verify CharacterMovement actually enters Swimming. Record the exact settings with a local screenshot before claiming compatibility.
Author BP_WaterRegion with WaterBodyId and surface bounds used by fishing; keep it distinct from the volume responsible for movement mode.
Assign DA_Swim_Default to BP_PlayerCharacter's swimming adapter and expose speed/shore permissions as defaults, not runtime writable UMG fields.
Test low banks, submerged stairs, bridge-over-water and gaps between neighboring volumes. Add a dry safe PlayerStart beside the test area.
failures: Client claims Dry while server capsule is submerged -> server mode wins; shore-only actions reject WrongMode.
Steep vertical bank -> Blocked/TooSteep; no implicit climb.
Volume destroyed or streamed out -> cancel dependent actions and recover to last validated safe position; log InvalidWater.
Swimming art missing -> visible declared fallback; collision/swim functionality remains testable.
tuning: Swimming speed 250 cm/s and no drowning are initial proposals. Underwater combat and mounted swimming are not part of the initial implementation.
observability: Show water ID, movement mode, floor result and action cancellation in diagnostics. Provide visual and text water-state cues; avoid requiring audio to notice danger.

title: Fixed camera, zoom, depth and occluder handling
purpose: Use a fixed three-quarter camera that follows the local pawn with clamped zoom. The camera is local presentation: it does not rotate collision, change server movement axes or confer visibility permission for attacks through walls.
fields: AzimuthDegrees=45 and ElevationDegrees=50; defaults, not free player rotation
FieldOfViewDegrees=35 for first perspective trial
ArmLengthCm: clamped 900..1600; zoom steps or analog wheel input
FollowLagSeconds: optional small local interpolation; no server position smoothing duplication
OcclusionCandidateTags: only authored environmental occluders
OpacityMinimum=0.25 and FadeSeconds=0.15; cosmetic proposal
commands: RestoreOccluders() -> Cleared; on travel, destruction, options change
flow: Local controller binds the camera to its currently possessed pawn, not PlayerController index 0 in shared server code.
Zoom input modifies the clamped local camera arm; fixed azimuth/elevation remain stable across facing changes.
Camera obstruction checks collect only tagged visual occluders between camera and avatar. Maintain reference counts when several traces request a fade.
Create per-client dynamic material instances or an explicitly client-local visibility solution; do not modify shared material assets or server collision.
When the actor is no longer an occluder, restore its original material parameters; teardown also restores everything.
Compare perspective and orthographic screenshots at identical apparent avatar size on slopes/bridges before choosing a projection; record results rather than declaring a universal winner.
editor_steps: Add a SpringArm and Camera under a stable camera root, separate from VisualRoot. Disable inherited control rotation and collision-driven facing rotation of the camera.
Assign DA_Camera_Default in BP_PlayerCharacter or the local controller camera adapter; tune FOV/arm length in L_ArtLab, not on a production biome first.
Create M_OccluderFade and MI_OccluderFade_Test with a local opacity parameter; use on a limited test wall/tree canopy before broader materials.
Bind IA_Zoom to SetZoomIntent and remove all camera rotation mappings. Add a zoom slider to WBP_Options with the same clamp.
Reopen all tagged occluder actors after material changes; verify camera fade does not disable weapon LOS or world collision.
failures: Two clients look through the same tree from different positions -> each has its own fade result, unchanged server collision.
Camera pawn destroyed during fade -> originals restored and no dangling material references.
Zoom to extremes -> no black borders, lost foot anchor or unacceptable sprite shimmer; clamp/tune on failure.
Enemy behind opaque wall -> soft target may show UI policy, but server attack LOS still rejects.
tuning: Perspective settings are trial values, not art-calibrated recommendations. Orthographic fallback must pass sorting, scale, shadow and height readability tests before adoption.
observability: Log only changed occluder sets in development. Camera shake, motion reduction, follow lag and zoom sensitivity are accessibility options; no network RPC per camera frame.

title: Input, UMG screen ownership, options and accessibility
purpose: Route keyboard/mouse and controller input to one local screen/input owner. UI displays snapshots and sends intents; it cannot pause a shared server, grant items, edit skill ownership or directly mutate replicated attributes.
fields: CurrentScreenId and ModalStack: client-only, bounded and cleared on travel
InputContextPriority: world=0, targeting=10, UI=100 proposed
TextScale=1.0; supported preview range 0.8..1.5
ReducedMotion, ColorIndependentTelegraphs, Subtitles, HoldToggleSprint: local options
ActionBindings: keyboard/mouse first, controller-ready; no mobile layout
NotificationId and ResultCode: structured text keys, not raw backend exception text
commands: CloseTopScreen(Reason) -> Closed; restore focus/input, not gameplay state
SubmitIntent(CommandKind, Payload) -> Pending|InputBlocked; delegates to owned controller/domain component
flow: Enhanced Input local-player subsystem installs IMC_World only for the owning local player. A dedicated server has no UMG or local input setup.
When inventory/dialogue opens, ScreenRouter saves focus and selects an explicit modal policy. The server world continues running.
Widget button handlers call exposed request functions and immediately enter Pending; they never subtract wallet text or item quantities optimistically as committed facts.
On accepted snapshot/receipt, update visible lists by stable item/quest identity and revision. On rejection show a localized reason and refresh affected data.
On possession change, unbind old delegates, bind new PlayerState/components when ready, and perform one initial snapshot refresh.
Travel/death/disconnect clears held actions and closes unsafe NPC/merchant/craft dialogs. Options may remain local, but no stale modal can issue a command against a new zone actor.
editor_steps: Create IA_Move(Axis2D), IA_Jump(Boolean), IA_Sprint(Boolean), IA_Dodge(Boolean), IA_Interact(Boolean), IA_Primary(Boolean), IA_TargetNext(Boolean), IA_Zoom(Axis1D) only when their consuming phases arrive.
Create IMC_World and IMC_UI. Map WASD, Space, Shift, a dodge key, E, mouse primary, Tab and wheel; add gamepad left stick, face buttons, triggers and D-pad counterparts with visible prompts.

Create Widget Blueprints from UserWidget, name interactive controls explicitly and set IsFocusable for navigable controls. Use scalable panels/anchors and reusable row widgets only where repeated behavior exists.

BP_RPGPlayerController creates ScreenRouter and the HUD only for IsLocalController. Never create UI in GameMode. Use input mode changes and focus explicitly; do not call SetGamePaused for a multiplayer menu.
For each screen wire OnClicked/selection events to custom intent functions and bind read-only delegates once. Prefer event updates to bound functions that poll every frame.
Test 1280x720 and 1920x1080, 150% text, keyboard only, controller only, no audio and a grayscale/colorblind review; localization keys must not be concatenated into English-only sentences.
failures: Open two modals repeatedly -> one well-defined top focus target, no duplicate delegates or RPCs.
Press confirm while request pending -> same command retry or no second request, never duplicate purchase.
Client opens Options during enemy attack -> world/other players continue; health still updates.
Close NPC UI during transfer -> old interaction token invalidated and focus restored after new possession.
tuning: Bindings and UI scaling ranges are proposals. Store graphics/input preferences locally; server-important settings and consent flags require explicit authoritative records. Provide remapping and conflict detection before release.
observability: Development overlay shows current input contexts, focus target, pending commands, state revision, ping and rejection codes. Production diagnostics hide secrets and internal stack traces.

title: Interaction targeting, range and modal cleanup
purpose: One player-owned interaction component resolves an interactable actor and asks the server to perform a specific action. NPCs, loot, nodes, banks and gates implement a narrow interaction interface without owning the player's inventory.
fields: TargetActorId: current replicated actor reference plus persistent source ID when applicable
InteractionVerb: allowlisted action tag such as Interact.Talk or Interact.Gather
InteractionRangeCm=250; per-definition override with server limit
InteractionNonce: server-issued short-lived context bound to character, target and zone epoch
EligibilityRevision: optional NPC/offer/node generation revision
RequiresLineOfSight=true except deliberately authored nonphysical UI actions
commands: ValidateInteractionContext(Nonce, CharacterSession) -> Valid|Expired|WrongZone; server custom helper
flow: Local overlap/trace selects a hint by distance/priority; display the intended verb and target name without asserting eligibility.
Client sends the actor reference and verb via its owned PlayerController or component RPC; never issue a Server RPC on an unowned resource actor.
Server resolves that actor in its own world, checks alive/session/readiness, capsule-to-target distance, LOS and supported interface/verb.
Domain owner returns an interaction context, such as a vendor quote or fishing action ID; it alone validates later state-changing commands.
UMG opens the corresponding screen using the context nonce. A later sale/craft/turn-in repeats range/session checks and does not rely on the initial conversation forever.
Leaving range, death, travel or actor destruction closes the context and cancels reversible actions. An already committed economic result is reconciled by receipt rather than undone by UI closure.
editor_steps: Define IRPGInteractable as a native UInterface with query/context and server-dispatch responsibilities. Expose the presentation query to Blueprint but keep authority checks native.
Add URPGInteractionComponent once to BP_PlayerCharacter. Route IA_Interact Started through BP_RPGPlayerController to the owned component.
Place InteractProbe in L_NetworkLab with an explicit collision/query volume and stable probe ID. Add a wall between it and one PlayerStart for LOS rejection.
Configure the interaction collision channel under Project Settings > Collision and document responses; sprite layers remain NoCollision.
Bind WBP_Notifications to structured rejection events; reopen gate/NPC/resource child Blueprints in their phases to implement the allowed verb and domain reference.
failures: Forged target from another zone -> InvalidTarget, no backend command.
Target destroyed between hint and request -> TargetGone; close hint safely.
Player sends NPC purchase while 1 km away -> OutOfRange even if UI remains open.
Late close after committed buy -> UI closes, owned item remains; no client-driven refund.
tuning: 250 cm is an initial range for a full-height avatar; tune to actual environment scale. Rate limit interaction starts independently from UI hover traces.
observability: Record target persistent ID, verb, session epoch and reason; no per-frame hover logs. Controller focus and screen-reader label should identify the same candidate as the visible prompt.

title: Dedicated-server bootstrap, possession and replication
purpose: Start a headless authority process and two independent clients early. GameMode controls admission/spawning in its one server world; PlayerState is an in-zone replicated actor, not a database or a cross-process singleton.
fields: ZoneInstanceId: backend-allocated UUID; one live authority lease
CharacterSessionEpoch: monotonic fencing integer; backend verified
CharacterRevision: monotonic durable snapshot version
SpawnReady: server state after content and snapshot validation
PublicPlayerState: display name, class, level, safe appearance; no private bag contents
ReplicationBaseline: generic actor/property/RPC; explicit relevancy and ownership
commands: AdmitPlayer(AdmissionProof, BuildVersion) -> Pending|Unauthorized|VersionMismatch; server admission contract
flow: Start Server_A without a local player. It registers zone instance/content version and obtains its backend lease before accepting durable actions.
Client_A and Client_B authenticate and connect using separate controllers/identities; admission validates tickets before a gameplay body is enabled.
GameMode creates or uses the intended PlayerState, hydrates authorized durable data through the server adapter, and spawns exactly one body at a valid PlayerStart.

Server possession initializes character components explicitly. Client OnRep/readiness observers may arrive in another order; a guarded readiness function binds UI/ASC only when all prerequisites exist.
Replicate movement and compact public presentation to relevant clients; replicate inventory/private quest details to the owner only.

On disconnect, cancel input-driven actions, apply the combat-logout policy, checkpoint accepted state, then release/revoke the lease through the backend. Reconnect always revalidates identity and epoch.
editor_steps: Use the official dedicated-server source-build route. Create native GameMode, GameState, PlayerController, PlayerState and Character bases in the developer's C++ project, compile, then create their BP children.

BP_ZoneGameMode Class Defaults: PlayerControllerClass=BP_RPGPlayerController, PlayerStateClass=BP_RPGPlayerState, GameStateClass=BP_ZoneGameState; gate DefaultPawn spawn until hydration. A project custom restart/spawn route must not duplicate automatic spawning.
Project Settings > Maps & Modes: set BP_RPGGameInstance and menu/gameplay defaults; L_NetworkLab World Settings uses BP_ZoneGameMode.

Enable replication on the native character/state actors and required components; assign ownership intentionally. Do not rely on Replicates to automatically replicate arbitrary variables or PaperZD graphs.

Place two separated PlayerStarts in L_NetworkLab and remove manually placed auto-possessed pawns. Start one dedicated process and two separate clients; PIE is a preliminary diagnostic, not packaged proof.
Reopen BP_RPGPlayerController to bind remote-safe diagnostics and local-only camera/input/UI. Server logs must identify distinct net connections and CharacterIds.
failures: Same character joins twice -> AlreadyOnline or controlled reconnect takeover with a new epoch, never two economic writers.
Client attempts to write wallet/XP property locally -> server state unchanged; owner snapshot corrects display.
Wrong content/build version -> VersionMismatch before possession; no partial inventory hydration.
Backend unavailable during admission -> remain connecting/error, not an unauthenticated fallback pawn.
Remove presentation component -> authority movement/combat still operates in headless tests.
tuning: Initial planning target 2 clients, then 8 and 16 per zone under measured load. Proposed 30 Hz server simulation and explicit actor update frequencies require profiling; they are not benchmarks.
observability: Separate connection ID, account pseudonymous audit ID, CharacterId, ZoneInstanceId and epoch. Record admission/hydration/spawn/ready transitions and owner-only data exposure checks.

title: Character persistence, schema, command receipts and sessions
purpose: Durability means accepted inventory, currency, quests and progression survive process loss. A UE zone keeps a short-lived authoritative session cache, while one authenticated backend commits durable relational records and audit receipts.
fields: CharacterId UUID; AccountId UUID; SchemaVersion integer; ContentVersion integer
CharacterRevision bigint >=0; SessionEpoch bigint >=1; OwnerZoneInstanceId UUID
CommandId UUID scoped to authenticated subject and operation; RequestHash immutable
Receipt: Pending|Committed|Rejected with immutable result and resulting revision
Quantities and BaseCurrency: bounded integers with database checks
OwnedItemId UUID for nonstackables; ItemDefinitionId stable string; no pointer serialization
LeaseExpiryUtc and LastDurableSafeLocation: backend-controlled values
flow: Zone adapter authenticates as a trusted server and includes CharacterId, zone ID, fencing epoch, expected revision, command ID and bounded validated payload.
Backend validates the server capability and current lease; it never trusts a client to select a privileged operation or pass a completed gameplay event.
Open a short database transaction; look up or insert the unique command record and compare request hash. A reused ID with different data rejects.
Lock all affected ownership/economy/source rows in a consistent order, revalidate constraints, apply all changes, increment revision and store result/audit/outbox rows atomically.
Commit before returning success. Zone applies the returned snapshot/delta on the game thread only if its session epoch and request generation still match.
Timeout means outcome unknown: suspend conflicting writes, query receipt or retry the identical command. A committed result is returned without consuming/granting again.
On restart, revoke expired leases, migrate supported records, and restore accepted facts; no widget or local SaveGame can override the snapshot.
editor_steps: Create the small backend as one service with routes grouped by domain, one relational database and migrations. Compare .NET 10 ASP.NET Core with TypeScript/Node; this guide chooses .NET 10 for typed contracts and a long support window, not because Node is invalid.

Define the database schema in sources/database-models.json and implement migrations in a separate backend repository; this documentation contains no production service implementation. Use a local isolated database and nonproduction accounts.
Add HTTP/JSON adapter dependencies to the native RPG module as needed after installed engine API review. Use asynchronous requests; never block the game thread on SQL or HTTP.

URPGCharacterServiceAdapter belongs to the server process lifecycle; client account adapter has separate capabilities. Keep endpoint allowlists and secrets in environment/deployment configuration, not Data Assets distributed to clients.

Create ServiceFixture_CharacterStore with committed, rejected, delayed-after-commit, stale-epoch and corrupted-record scenarios. Reopen ARPGZoneGameMode to require successful hydration before possession.
Expose immutable snapshot getters/delegates to Blueprint, not arbitrary SQL or SetCurrency functions. Test adapter callbacks after actor teardown and server travel.
failures: Lost response after commit -> GetCommandReceipt returns one original result; no second grant.
Same command ID/different payload -> IdempotencyConflict; original receipt remains unchanged.
Old source server uses epoch N after transfer to N+1 -> SessionFenced; no write.
Concurrent withdraw/craft using same item -> consistent lock/revision policy accepts only a valid serial outcome.
Unknown schema/content ID -> InvalidRecord or UnsupportedContentVersion; quarantine and show safe login error, not silently delete items.
Database serialization/deadlock retry -> retry the entire transaction under bounded policy, never only the final reward insert.
tuning: Proposed command payload limit 32 KiB, bounded retry with jitter, 30-second session lease renewed every 10 seconds. Tune under actual load and failure tests; no unbounded in-memory reward queue.
observability: Ledger fields include command/character/zone/epoch/revision/reason/definition IDs and deltas. Exclude secrets, raw provider proofs and unnecessary chat content. Backups require restore drills, not merely successful backup jobs.

title: Biome servers, loading screens and fenced handoff
fixture: L_Rillmere / Gate_East / L_Thornweald / Gate_West / Server_A / Server_B
purpose: A player walks through a registered road gate and connects to a different server process while other players remain in the source zone. Internal world streaming can reduce one map's memory use but cannot perform this identity/session handoff.
fields: GateId: stable authored ID; SourceZoneId, DestinationZoneId, DestinationEntranceId
TransferId UUID; SourceEpoch bigint; DestinationEpoch=SourceEpoch+1 on redemption
SnapshotRevision: last accepted durable character revision
DestinationReservationId and CapacityExpiryUtc: backend-managed
SignedTicketClaims: issuer,audience,account,character,transfer,destination,revision,expiry,nonce
TicketUsed: one-use backend record; signature alone is not replay prevention
commands: PrepareTransfer(CharacterId, Epoch, Revision, Destination) -> ReservationAndTicket|Rejected; backend proposal
AcknowledgeArrival(TransferId, Epoch) -> Completed; backend/source cleanup notification
flow: Player interaction reaches source server; verify gate actor, range/LOS, destination/return entrance, character eligibility and no disallowed combat/death state.
Freeze new economic starts and drain/reconcile accepted commands. Persist current accepted snapshot with expected revision; never serialize a client UI inventory.
Backend reserves a destination instance with free capacity and records Preparing transfer state under the current fenced character lease. On failure unfreeze source safely.

Create a short-lived signed ticket bound to account, character, destination and revision. Deliver it through the authenticated session channel; avoid placing bearer credentials in logs or long-lived URLs.
Source instructs only the owning controller to ClientTravel to the allocated server endpoint using absolute travel. A loading screen spans disconnect/connect; other controllers do not travel.

Destination validates identity/ticket/reservation, then atomically consumes the ticket and changes session ownership/epoch in the backend. Old source writes immediately become fenced, even before visual acknowledgement.
Destination loads the agreed snapshot, spawns one body guarded by CharacterId+epoch, restores persistent facts without replaying grants, and enables input only after hydration/possession readiness.

Arrival acknowledgement retires the frozen source body and reservation. If destination crashes after redemption, recovery obtains a later epoch; it never reuses a consumed token or reactivates old authority.
editor_steps: Author DA_Zone_Rillmere and DA_Zone_Thornweald with exact map soft paths and entrance IDs. Place BP_ZoneGate actors as Gate_East and Gate_West with reciprocal links and safe spawn transforms away from overlap retrigger.
Run separate Server_A and Server_B processes on different game ports. Register both with the same development backend; do not use whole-server ServerTravel to test a single-player gate.
Create WBP_Loading through the process-local client screen/session owner, not the source pawn. Its state persists while that pawn/controller is replaced.

Reopen BP_RPGPlayerController: clear held input and close dialogue/vendor/craft contexts on Prepare; route connection/network failure to RecoverTransfer. The backend decides the safe next destination.

Use the engine ClientTravel API for an external connection. Transition maps/seamless ServerTravel are for moving a server's clients together; streaming cells stay within a server world. Exact secure admission transport must be verified in installed engine/provider configuration.
Add fixtures for full destination, expired reservation, duplicate ticket, stale snapshot, source crash before redemption and destination crash after redemption.
failures: Client_A travels while Client_B remains -> A arrives at Gate_West, B stays in Rillmere and Server_A remains alive.
Source crash before redeem -> backend resolves Preparing state and reconnects with one valid lease, no lost committed craft.
Duplicate ticket -> AlreadyUsed; no second pawn or reward replay.
Destination full -> ZoneFull before departure when possible; source unfreezes or recovery sends to safe hub with a new valid reservation.
Old source tries to sell after redemption -> SessionFenced and no ledger entry.
NPC UI reply arrives after travel -> ignored by generation/zone check; never opens an old merchant in the new zone.
tuning: Proposed ticket TTL 60 seconds and reservation TTL 90 seconds. Spawn cooldown/offset prevents portal ping-pong. These require latency and capacity measurements; loading screens do not imply instant distributed atomicity.
observability: Trace TransferId across source, backend and destination. Record prepare/redeem/hydrate/ack timestamps, epoch and revision. Keep signatures/tickets out of ordinary logs; require secure admission transport before public deployment.

title: GAS ownership, attributes, costs and prediction
purpose: Use one Gameplay Ability System stack for health, mana, stamina, abilities, costs, cooldowns and effects. A player's ASC lives on PlayerState during one zone session; the current body is its avatar. An ordinary enemy owns its ASC on its Character.
fields: AttributeSet: Health/MaxHealth, Mana/MaxMana, Stamina/MaxStamina, Power, Armor and resistance attributes
AbilitySpec handles: transient per ASC, not durable skill IDs
GrantedAbilityIds and purchased talents: durable definitions reconstructed after transfer
OwnerActor=PlayerState; AvatarActor=current PlayerCharacter; enemy owner/avatar=enemy
PredictionKey: GAS mechanism for supported predicted actions, not an economic command ID
LongCooldownExpiryUtc: durable policy for cooldowns that must not reset on zone change
ActionSequenceId: compact presentation identity distinct from a database receipt
commands: InitializeAbilityActorInfo(Owner, Avatar) -> Ready|MissingOwner; project lifecycle wrapper around inspected GAS API
GrantBuildAbilities(BuildRevision) -> Granted|InvalidDefinition; server only, idempotent by current grant set
RequestAbility(AbilityInputTag, TargetIntent) -> Predicted|Rejected; local input plus server validation
flow: On server possession, obtain the PlayerState ASC, validate hydrated build, initialize actor info with PlayerState as owner and Character as avatar, then apply default attributes and granted abilities once.

On the owning client, PlayerState replication and possession readiness both call one guarded initialization path. Do not assume BeginPlay/OnRep order; rebind after respawn and clear old avatar delegates.
Input tags resolve to granted ability specs. Use supported GAS local prediction for responsiveness, while the server rechecks costs, tags, target/range/LOS and cooldown.

Server commits accepted GAS cost/cooldown and applies effects. Rejected predictions are reconciled by GAS and the project's UI/visual observer; never maintain a second manually predicted health balance.
ASC delegates produce read-only attribute updates and semantic action cues for PaperZD; no PlayMontageAndWait dependency is assumed for sprites.

On death cancel transient abilities and reinitialize the new avatar; on cross-server transfer create a new ASC and rebuild from durable definition IDs, not serialized object pointers/spec handles. Persist selected long cooldown expiries under a declared policy.
editor_steps: Enable Gameplay Ability System and Gameplay Tags dependencies in the C++ project. Add the needed GameplayAbilities, GameplayTags and GameplayTasks module dependencies using the installed engine conventions.

Define URPGAttributeSet and URPGAbilitySystemComponent; PlayerState owns both and the Character implements IAbilitySystemInterface by returning that same ASC. Do not add another player ASC to the pawn.

Create DA_CombatRules_Default and the initial GE_DefaultAttributes, GE_Damage, GE_Healing, GE_Cost and GE_Cooldown assets from their intended GAS bases. Separate authored effects from live active-effect state.
Implement server possession and owning-client replicated-PlayerState readiness hooks. Check InitAbilityActorInfo and related API signatures in the installed 5.8.3 headers before compiling.
Configure owner/public effect replication deliberately and measure PlayerState update rates; a common mixed-mode choice is only adopted after its owner-chain requirements are verified.
Reopen BP_PlayerCharacter movement adapters to consume the ASC's stamina; reopen WBP_HUD and WBP_ActionBar to bind attribute/cooldown delegates and display server rejection text.
failures: Respawn twice -> exactly one ability grant set and one set of UI delegates.
Predicted cast with insufficient server mana -> rejection restores local presentation/cost expectation; no enemy damage.
PlayerState arrives after pawn -> HUD waits, then binds once; no null ASC access.
Zone transfer during cast -> cast canceled; a long cooldown does not reset merely because a new ASC is created.
Remove all sprite assets -> server costs/cooldowns/hits still work.
tuning: Initial health 100, mana 100, stamina 100 are fixtures, not class balance. No global cooldown initially; selected abilities may share an authored cooldown tag. Test update frequency rather than copying a default from another project.
observability: Diagnostics show ASC owner/avatar, granted definition IDs, active tags, prediction rejection and attribute revision. GAS is not an inventory, quest, authentication or persistence service.

title: Soft targets, utility targeting, LOS and telegraphs
purpose: Soft targeting helps select an enemy or ally, but a selection does not guarantee a hit. Melee/projectile/area rules still use the server's current positions, collision, faction and ability definition.
fields: TargetId: transient actor/network identity, resolved on server
TargetPointCm: finite world vector constrained to range and valid surface
TargetPolicy: Hostile|Friendly|Self|Ground; authored per ability
MaxRangeCm and RadiusCm: definition values, not UI inputs
RequiresLOS=true; trace channel and occlusion policy recorded per ability
TargetRevision/ActionSequenceId: reject stale actor reuse
commands: CycleTarget(Direction) -> Candidate; visible candidate set, controller-ready
ConfirmGroundTarget(Point) -> AbilityRequest; client intent, server rechecks
flow: Mouse/cycle input chooses a readable target or ground reticle, with name/health from public replicated state.
When the player activates an ability, submit the intended actor/point and ability ID; do not send a claimed damage amount or hit result.
Server verifies actor existence, alive state, hostile/friendly policy, distance from approved origin, LOS and point bounds.
A cast may revalidate at impact/end according to its authored tracking policy; moving out of range during a cast is not automatically a guaranteed hit.
For an area effect, server queries candidate actors, filters/deduplicates them and applies effect eligibility; reticle graphics have no damage authority.
Replicate accepted telegraph center/radius/start/end and semantic shape ID so remote clients show the same warning even if their render frame differs.
editor_steps: Add URPGTargetingComponent to BP_PlayerCharacter and route mouse selection/IA_TargetNext through the local controller; keep authoritative validation callable from GAS.
Author DA_Targeting_Default and an explicit targeting profile for each initial ability. Add a behind-wall dummy and friendly character fixture.
Create WBP_TargetFrame and a ground-reticle visual with noncolliding components; bind to target lifetime and public health delegates.
Set collision query channels to block intended world geometry and ignore cosmetic sprite layers. Display debug traces only in development.
Reopen the ability definitions to assign target policy, range, LOS, retarget behavior and cancellation reason; do not infer these from weapon art.
failures: Target dies before server validation -> TargetDead; no cost under precommit-rejection policy.
Client changes radius/range in packet -> ignored/rejected; server definition wins.
Ground target inside inaccessible geometry -> InvalidTargetPoint; reticle becomes invalid before confirm where possible.
Target hidden by local canopy fade -> server wall LOS still determines eligibility.
tuning: Proposed melee range 220 cm, ranged range 1800 cm and ground radius 250 cm for fixtures. No PvP targeting initially. Target assistance must not secretly extend server range.
observability: Show a reason-specific reticle state, shape outline and countdown text; no color-only telegraphs. Log invalid vectors and excessive target requests with rate limits.

title: Melee sweeps, server projectiles and hit deduplication
purpose: Spatial attacks use real 3D collision queries while sprites communicate their timing. The server owns the active window, projectile spawn and effect application, and records which targets have already been attempted for each execution.
fields: AttackExecutionId: server sequence scoped to attacker session
WindupSeconds, ActiveSeconds, RecoverySeconds: authored gameplay timing, independent of source PNG timing
MeleeQuery: swept capsule/box path, range and forward arc
AttemptedTargetIds: transient set for one execution; add before invoking effect
ProjectileId, SpawnOrigin, InitialVelocity, LifetimeSeconds: server-generated
DamageDefinitionId and EffectContext: immutable accepted attack parameters
commands: AdvanceMeleeWindow(ExecutionId, PreviousTime, CurrentTime) -> HitAttempts; server timer/tick under explicit ownership
flow: GAS accepts the ability and creates one hit execution with a gameplay time interval and accepted stats/context.
Server advances windup/active/recovery on its own clock. If a frame crosses the complete active interval, perform the bounded swept query for the crossed segment instead of losing the hit window.
Normalize overlap/trace results to target actors, check collision/LOS/faction and insert target identity into AttemptedTargetIds before invoking damage.

For ranged attacks, spawn a server-owned projectile with collision and movement, ignore the instigator and resolve blocking impact once; clients may predict a cosmetic projectile that is reconciled to the accepted one.
Damage/healing effects apply through the one GAS effect path. Cosmetic PaperZD notifies may add sounds but cannot call ResolveImpact or release authoritative cooldowns.
Cancel execution on death/interruption/invalid avatar and destroy or invalidate remaining projectiles under their authored lifetime policy.
editor_steps: Create ARPGProjectile from Actor with a collision root and ProjectileMovementComponent; use a separate noncolliding visual child. Set server replication/velocity policy and lifetime.
Create BP_Projectile_TrainingArrow and BP_Projectile_ArcSpark with their visual definitions; no arrows or magic effects are claimed in the supplied ZIP.
Add URPGHitResolver to authoritative characters and expose only debug geometry/tuning via definitions; clients cannot submit arbitrary effect specs.
Create the initial melee and projectile ability definitions with explicit active windows, origins and query shapes. Origin comes from validated avatar/weapon anchor, not the client mouse ray start.
Place dummies at near/far distances and a blocking wall in L_NetworkLab. Reopen GAS abilities to call the resolver at gameplay times and presentation adapter to observe the same execution ID.
failures: Two components on one target overlap -> one damage attempt per execution.
Packet replay or duplicated overlap -> AlreadyAttempted, no extra damage.
Projectile hits wall before enemy -> destroyed/blocked; no damage through wall.
Attacker dies in windup -> Canceled; missed animation completion cannot leave a permanent attack lock.
Client sends impossible muzzle origin -> InvalidOrigin; server uses approved location or rejects.
tuning: Training melee windup 0.15 s, active 0.10 s, recovery 0.30 s; arrow speed 1800 cm/s, lifetime 3 s. Values are proposals. Lag compensation is not silently added; evaluate a bounded server-history approach only after baseline measurements.
observability: Trace execution IDs, attempted targets, collision hits, authoritative origin and rejection reasons. Client visual hit feedback distinguishes predicted contact from confirmed damage.

title: Damage, healing, resistances, status effects and interruption
purpose: Apply combat math and status rules once, through GAS-backed authoritative execution. Healing, damage types, criticals, buffs/debuffs, crowd control and cast interruption are authored rules, not hardcoded UI labels or sprite animation side effects.
fields: DamageType: Physical|Fire|Frost|Storm|Spirit; authored extensible tags
RawAmount=max(0, BaseAmount + Power*Coefficient); reject nonfinite inputs
ArmorReduction=Armor/(Armor+100+10*AttackerLevel), clamp 0..0.75 for fixture
ElementalResistance: clamp -0.25..0.75; outgoing/incoming modifiers apply in documented order
CriticalChance: clamp 0..1; CriticalMultiplier>=1; server roll
EffectStackPolicy: Refresh|AddStackToCap|Independent|RejectDuplicate
InterruptPolicy: movement/damage/hard-control tags per ability; effect expiry uses server time
flow: Read accepted attacker stats and target mitigation under the definition's snapshot/dynamic policy; never calculate different authoritative formulas in UI, Character and ability.
Compute raw amount, outgoing modifiers, mitigation/resistance, critical outcome and incoming modifiers in the documented order, then clamp finite bounds and health resources.
Server applies the resulting GAS effect; death is detected once by the health/defeat owner rather than each damage source.
Healing validates friendly policy and caps at missing health; overheal may be recorded but is not extra XP or threat unless explicitly authored.
Status application evaluates immunity, stacking, duration, periodic tick ownership and interruption. A canceled channel stops future ticks but does not undo already committed impacts.
Replicate effect tags/resource outcomes and semantic cues; UI shows duration from server time and clears stale icons on avatar replacement.
editor_steps: Author GE_Damage, GE_Healing and representative burn/slow/stun effects with definitions/tags. Keep periodic damage on the authority and use stable effect context for credit.
Set training dummy armor to 20, attacker level to 1 and raw physical amount to 20: expected pre-round damage is 20*(1-20/130), approximately 16.923; record the chosen rounding policy.
Create an interruptible Arcanist cast and a Warden heal targeting Ally_A. Configure cancel tags and remove skeletal montage prerequisites.
Bind WBP_HUD resource bars/status rows to ASC delegates. Tooltips explain damage type and resistance without independently recomputing hidden server rolls.
Reopen death, threat and combat-log consumers: damage accepted emits one verified event; no UI event can grant kill credit.
failures: NaN/negative/unbounded input -> InvalidDefinition/Payload, no attribute corruption.
Heal dead target without resurrection ability -> TargetDead.
Apply same nonstacking effect twice -> refresh/reject per policy, not accidental double periodic ticks.
Interrupt stale action sequence -> Stale; current new cast continues.
Disconnect/zone travel -> short transient effects canceled; long expiry effects restored only under explicit durable policy.
tuning: No PvP crowd-control diminishing returns initially. For repeated PvE stun, propose boss immunity tags and a per-target recent-control budget only when encounter tests justify it. Critical and mitigation values are balance proposals.
observability: Combat log includes damage type, amount, mitigation, critical flag and source execution ID, not raw hidden RNG seeds. Provide text/icons for effects and a reduced-motion option.

title: NavMesh AI, perception, threat, leash and evade
purpose: Server-owned AI moves a capsule over actual 3D walkable surfaces. Use AIController, Behavior Tree, Blackboard, AI Perception and navigation before considering a second decision framework.
fields: Blackboard: TargetActor, HomeLocation, PatrolIndex, HasLOS, InAttackRange, IsEvading
ThreatByCharacterId: server-only finite nonnegative values; eligible source context
PerceptionRadiusCm=1800; LeashRadiusCm=3000; HomeLocation authoritative spawn
AttackDefinitionIds: authored choices with range/cooldown/role restrictions
LastReachableTargetPosition: transient navigation hint, not permission to attack through walls
FactionDisposition: Passive|Defensive|Aggressive rules; boss overrides explicit
commands: RequestAttackFromAI(AbilityId, Target) -> Accepted|Cooldown|NoLOS; uses same ability validation
EnterEvade(Reason) -> Resetting; cancel combat/credit under declared reset policy
flow: Spawn controller possesses the enemy Character and initializes definition, ASC and Blackboard before running the Behavior Tree.
Perception updates candidate targets; a target selector combines disposition/threat/leash rules and writes one Blackboard TargetActor.
Behavior Tree moves with navigation, chooses attack when range/LOS/cooldown permit, and calls the same authoritative ability stack as player attacks.
Damage/healing contribution emits verified threat; threat does not come from client UI selection or proximity alone.
If target is unreachable/outside leash or combat stalls, enter Evade: cancel attacks/projectiles owned by this reset, clear threat/credit according to policy and navigate home.

After reaching a valid home floor, restore health under reset policy and resume patrol. Defeated state instead hands off to the unique defeat/loot record; it cannot evade back to life after rewards committed.
editor_steps: Create BB_Enemy and BT_Enemy with priority branches Defeated, Evade, Combat, Patrol, Idle. Create project BT tasks only for domain operations not supplied by standard movement/wait tasks.
Create BP_EnemyAIController from ARPGEnemyAIController and assign perception plus Blackboard/BehaviorTree references. Configure sensing affiliations deliberately.

BP_Enemy_Mossfang derives from the native enemy Character, uses a capsule, CharacterMovement, ASC and noncolliding sprite presentation. Set AI Controller Class and auto-possession policy for spawned AI.
Place NavMeshBoundsVolume over all intended test surfaces and build navigation. Press the Editor navigation visualization toggle and inspect ramps, bridge decks, stairs and gaps.
Place Encounter_WestRoad with DA_Enemy_Mossfang, a home point and patrol route. Test melee pursuer, ranged sentry and passive wildlife as definition variants, not separate copied AI stacks.
Use StateTree only after a measured maintenance/performance comparison and a migration decision; do not run two behavior authorities on one enemy.
failures: Target behind unreachable ledge -> pursue/reposition or evade; no platformer X-axis chase heuristic.
Player kites beyond leash -> encounter resets safely and no reward is emitted.
Target disconnects -> choose remaining valid threat or reset; no null-target attack.
Two clients damage one enemy -> server threat/credit are consistent; client order does not determine final ledger identity.
Navmesh missing on bridge -> NavigationFailure diagnostic; do not teleport through geometry to hide the error.
tuning: Radius/timing values are initial fixtures. Proposed stalled-path timeout 5 seconds with bounded retries. Threat coefficients and healer threat need party tests; no assumption of MMO-scale AI count.
observability: Use server AI debugger/Blackboard inspection and threat logs gated to development. Replicate only readable intent/telegraphs and movement, not the entire Behavior Tree or threat map.

title: Enemy spawning, defeat ledger, XP and group credit
purpose: An encounter owns spawn generations and legitimate participation. Defeat creates a durable receipt before XP/loot success is announced, so corpse reload or server restart cannot reward the same enemy twice.
fields: EncounterId and SpawnSiteId: stable authored IDs
SpawnGeneration: monotonic generation for one life; paired with ZoneInstanceId/world epoch
DefeatId: unique zone/site/generation record; database uniqueness
Contribution: verified damage/heal/support events with CharacterId and time
EligiblePartySnapshot: party revision, nearby alive/participating members under declared policy
XPReward: integer definition value; allocation is deterministic given eligibility
RespawnAtUtc: persisted or explicit reset policy, never recomputed as immediate on reload
flow: Zone encounter owner validates an authored site and creates one enemy generation, recording its stable source identity.
Server hit/effect events update contribution; nearby idle alts are not eligible solely because their UI shows a target.
At health zero, atomically transition to DefeatedPendingCommit once and freeze further attacks/reset; calculate eligibility from current authenticated character/party snapshots.

Submit the defeat command with unique DefeatId. Backend persists defeat, per-character XP allocations, reward entitlements and receipt together; later loot materialization references these entitlements.
Only committed result updates PlayerState XP/level and corpse/loot access. Timeout preserves Pending and reconciles the original command, not a new defeat.
Respawn uses a new generation after the configured interval. Old corpse/reward commands reference the old generation and cannot grant from the new enemy.
editor_steps: Create DA_Encounter_WestRoad with a stable site list, enemy definition, respawn policy and reward rule. Populate one site first.
Place BP_EncounterSpawner and its patrol/home markers in L_Rillmere; server only spawns live enemies. Clients never run the spawning timer.
Introduce DB_encounter_resolutions, DB_command_receipts and the minimal Party_AB fixture before enabling group rewards. Full party invitations/chat remain Phase 19.
Reopen URPGEffectRules to emit verified contribution to the encounter owner; reopen ARPGEnemyCharacter's death path to call FinalizeDefeat once.
Reopen WBP_HUD to observe committed XP revision. Display pending reward notification during a backend delay rather than an uncommitted item count.
failures: Two simultaneous lethal hits -> one DefeatId, one set of allocations.
Corpse unloaded/reloaded -> existing reward state restored, no second XP.
Kill then database timeout after commit -> receipt query restores original allocations.
Evade before defeat -> no XP/loot, contribution cleared by reset policy.
Client forges contribution -> ignored; only zone-authorized verified events accepted.
tuning: Training enemy gives 40 XP. Eligible two-person party splits 20/20 initially; contribution proximity proposal 3000 cm and recent activity 30 seconds. Personal loot allocations avoid early need/greed UI; balancing may revise this policy.
observability: Log defeat identity, eligibility snapshot, XP allocations and receipt revision. Track pending-reward age and duplicate suppression. Database outage policy stops new reward-producing encounters once bounded pending capacity is reached.

title: Death, shrine respawn and reconnect policy
purpose: Death replaces the combat body state without wiping progression. A safe shrine/bind point provides recovery; a client reconnect is not allowed to reset inventory, undo a death penalty or refresh all resources for free.
fields: DeathId: unique character/session/body-life identifier
BindPointId: unlocked safe entrance or shrine; persisted
DurabilityPenaltyPercent=0.05; configurable and rounded under one rule
Persistent facts retained: XP, quest progress, inventory, equipped identities, currencies
Transient policy: cancel casts/gather/fish/trade preparation, clear short harmful statuses
RespawnResourcePolicy: full health, 50% mana/stamina proposal; long cooldowns preserved
CombatLogoutGraceSeconds=15 proposal; server body remains vulnerable during grace
commands: CommitDeathPenalty(CommandId, DeathId) -> Applied|AlreadyApplied; backend economic command
flow: Authoritative health reaches zero once; recovery owner marks dead, cancels actions and notifies encounter/group systems.
Backend command applies configured durability/currency policy at most once. No inventory destruction or XP rollback is allowed by the default.
WBP_Death observes death/penalty readiness and shows a clear respawn option; it never resets attributes directly.
Server verifies a safe unlocked bind point and spawns/repossesses one replacement body; PlayerState ASC rebinds to that avatar.
Restore persistent inventory/quests/XP unchanged, apply respawn resource/status policy and retain selected long cooldown expiry records.
A disconnected live body follows combat grace and checkpoint rules. Rejoining restores the committed alive/dead state; it cannot choose an old local save to avoid death.
editor_steps: Place Shrine_Hearthford outside enemy/resource collision and register its SpawnPointId in DA_Zone_Rillmere. Add a kill-floor recovery fallback per zone.
Create DA_Recovery_Default and WBP_Death; the Respawn button calls the controller's validated recovery request, then waits for possession/readiness.
Reopen GAS initialization to distinguish initial login, new body after death and cross-zone reconstruction. Do not regrant starting items or duplicate abilities on each respawn.
Reopen gathering/fishing/dialogue/trade components to cancel transient work by matching action/offer ID; committed results remain durable.
Place Hazard_Test in a marked lab-only corner, not on the production PlayerStart. Run lethal and simultaneous-disconnect scenarios with Client_B observing.
failures: Repeated death callback -> one DeathId/penalty.
Disconnect after penalty committed but before respawn -> reconnect still dead/respawn-ready, no second penalty.
Bind point missing or map unavailable -> validated zone safe-hub fallback, not arbitrary client coordinates.
Inventory full at death -> no item loss; durability changes affect equipped instances only.
Old pawn sends late RPC -> WrongAvatar/SessionFenced; new body unaffected.
tuning: Default penalty is 5% equipped durability loss, no currency subtraction; repairs create the modest economic cost. Proposed respawn delay 5 seconds. These can be tuned but must not become a rollback mechanic.
observability: Record DeathId, penalty receipt and body-life identifier. Death UI is keyboard/controller accessible, has text instructions and no required rapid reaction.

title: Levels, derived stats and profession progression
purpose: Character XP/levels and profession skill are separate durable tracks. The level cap is data-defined; derived combat attributes are rebuilt from class growth, level, equipment, talents and valid effects rather than saved as competing authoritative totals.
fields: CharacterXP: cumulative nonnegative bigint; no float XP
LevelCap=50; strictly increasing authored cumulative thresholds
Level: derived from XP and threshold table, persisted only as validated cache if needed
SkillPointsEarned/Spent: derived/recorded under talent rules; cannot become negative
ProfessionXP: map by profession definition ID; independent thresholds
DerivedStatInputs: class, level, equipped item revisions, purchased talents; no UI-owned values
commands: ResolveLevel(CumulativeXP, CurveVersion) -> Level; deterministic pure rule
ApplyProfessionXP(ProfessionId, VerifiedCommand) -> Updated|Rejected; part of gather/craft/fish transaction
flow: A verified defeat/quest/gather/craft/fish command produces a durable XP delta under its domain rule, never from a UI animation.
Backend applies delta once and validates the threshold-table version; level changes and earned skill-point changes are returned in the same result.
Zone updates progression cache and rebuilds derived attribute inputs through the one GAS initialization/modifier path.
Health/max-resource changes follow an explicit policy: preserve current percentage on a max-stat rebuild while clamping bounds; do not fully heal on equipment swap.
Owner UI displays XP/level and a level-up cue keyed to receipt/revision; remote nameplates see only public level.
At cap, stop character XP progression under the chosen cap policy while allowing professions/quests/items to remain useful; no impossible prerequisite beyond cap.
editor_steps: Author DT_LevelThresholds with rows 1..50 and strictly increasing cumulative XP. Start with a small test threshold so Slice B can prove leveling, then restore catalog values.
Create DA_Progression_Default linking class growth and threshold data. Do not hardcode level 50 in widgets.
Add URPGProgressionComponent to PlayerState after native compilation; it owns in-zone read-only projections of durable progression.
Bind WBP_Stats and HUD XP display to progression delegates, and enemy/quest reward owners to the backend receipt pathway.
Reopen equipment/talent/GAS consumers to call RebuildDerivedStats after committed build revisions; do not stack a second permanent effect on every refresh.
failures: Replay XP receipt -> unchanged cumulative XP.
Threshold table contains duplicate/decreasing row -> content validator fails before admission.
Equip/unequip repeatedly -> identical final stats, no accumulated hidden bonuses.
At level 50 receive XP -> declared cap result, no level 51 or negative bar.
Profession reward after reconnect -> one profession increment tied to original gather/craft/fish command.
tuning: Suggested early tuning curve: XP needed for next level = 100 + 30*(level-1)^2; use a Data Table and playtest pacing. This is not a balanced 50-level campaign.
observability: Log XP source entitlement and input build revision. Stats tooltip separates base, level, equipment, talent and temporary modifiers; do not reveal hidden server anti-abuse values.

title: Item definitions, instances, rarities and generated affixes
purpose: An authored item definition says what an item can be. An owned gear instance identifies one particular item; a stack row stores a quantity. A world pickup or resource node is a separate source, not the owned item itself.
fields: ItemDefinitionId: stable item.* ID, content version and type family
OwnedItemId: server-generated UUID for nonstackable gear; immutable across bank/trade/zone moves
Rarity: Common|Uncommon|Rare|Epic|Legendary; authored/drop-generated, not UI color authority
ItemLevel and MinimumCharacterLevel: nonnegative integers; class/profession gates optional
MaxStack: positive integer for stackables; gear MaxStack=1
AffixDefinitionIds and rolled values: valid family/range only, rolled once on server
BindingPolicy: Unbound|BindOnPickup|BindOnEquip|AccountBound; owner restrictions
DurabilityCurrent/Maximum: bounded integers; set ID and weapon-hand requirement authored
commands: GenerateOwnedItem(AuthorizedRewardSource, FamilyId, RollContext) -> ItemInstance|InvalidFamily; server/backend coordinated
flow: Content author creates a definition with stable ID, type, stack policy, rarity, level requirements, price basis and optional visual mapping.
A committed loot/craft/shop reward requests an item from an allowed family; server selects a permitted definition/affix outcome and records the resolved result in the command transaction.
Generate one owned UUID for nonstackable gear and persist rolled properties; retries retrieve the stored result rather than rerolling.
Inventory/equipment/bank/trade move the same instance identity and enforce binding/ownership without recreating it.
UI resolves display text/icons/rarity styling from definitions and instance values; it does not compute a new random affix on hover.
Unknown content version blocks unsafe mutation and shows an explicit unavailable-item view; migration maps old IDs without silently replacing rare items.
editor_steps: Create native URPGItemDefinition from PrimaryDataAsset and the catalog resolver; expose authored fields EditDefaultsOnly/BlueprintReadOnly and validation errors.
In Phase 05 define minimal backend item identity records for reward/transfer proof. Author the actual starter material/gear instances in Phase 09, not hundreds of unused shells in Phase 00.
Create DA_Item_CopperOre, DA_Item_AshLog, DA_Item_RiverDace, DA_Item_HealingDraught, DA_Item_IronHatchet, DA_Item_TrainingSword, DA_Item_TrainingShield and DA_Item_WovenCloak as worked examples.
Create WBP_ItemTooltip with name, type, rarity text, requirements, modifiers, binding, durability and comparison fields. Show stat-only equipment clearly when no visual overlay exists.
Reopen catalogs and content validation: every referenced loot/recipe/vendor item ID must resolve before the zone enables that feature.
failures: Replaced item UUID in sell request -> ItemNotOwned or StaleItem; no sale of a different slot occupant.
Affix outside family/range -> InvalidAffix; content or request rejected.
Negative/overflow stack quantity -> InvalidQuantity; no arithmetic wrap.
Unknown definition after patch -> UnsupportedContentVersion and quarantine policy, not data deletion.
tuning: Rarity weights, item levels, affix ranges and prices are proposals. No carry weight. Gear family can opt out of affixes entirely; deterministic starter gear is easier to test.
observability: Ledger records item UUID, definition, source entitlement and affix result. Tooltips use text/icon distinctions as well as rarity color and support localization/long names.

title: Inventory bags, stacks, capacity and atomic moves
purpose: Inventory is a bounded collection of stack/instance records. UI drag/drop requests a move; the backend commits ownership and capacity changes. Slot index alone is not a safe identity for a mutable item.
fields: InventoryRevision bigint; ContainerId UUID; SlotIndex 0..Capacity-1
Capacity=16 initially; expansions are durable entitlements
SlotPayload: Empty|Stack(DefinitionId,Quantity,BindingKey)|Instance(OwnedItemId)
Stack compatibility: same definition, binding and relevant variant; quantities <= MaxStack
ExpectedSourceItemId/StackRevision: optimistic check to prevent slot-replacement races
ReservedCapacity: only used by explicitly modeled pending/escrow operations; no invisible duplicate bag
commands: RequestMove(CommandId, SourceContainer, SourceSlot, ExpectedItem, DestinationSlot, Quantity) -> Moved|StaleItem|NoSpace
PreviewCapacity(PlannedRewards) -> Fits|NoSpace; UI hint, repeated authoritatively
flow: Player drags a stable item view or requests split quantity; UI sends expected identity/revision and destination, then marks involved slots pending.
Server checks owned session, request bounds, allowed container types and action state; backend locks character/container rows and resolves the actual current source.
Validate stack compatibility, available quantity, destination capacity and binding. Simulate all deltas before applying any.
Commit source/destination changes, inventory revision and receipt together. For a swap validate both sides; never remove the source before discovering the destination cannot accept it.
Zone updates owner-only replicated projection; WBP_Inventory reconciles by identity/revision and restores pending focus after result.
After timeout/reconnect, query receipt and snapshot. Do not recreate dragged items or trust locally cached slot contents.
editor_steps: Create URPGInventoryComponent on PlayerState for owner-only in-zone inventory projection. Persistent rows remain in the backend.
Create DA_Inventory_Default with 16 slots and explicit expansion rules; WBP_Inventory builds slots from capacity, not a fixed six-slot legacy panel.
Add item-row/slot UMG widgets only as reusable presentational children; their OnDrop handlers call inventory requests, not SetArrayElem on the authoritative model.
Seed Bag16 with one full ore stack, one partial stack, a sword instance and one final empty slot. Add a full-bag variation for capacity tests.
Reopen loot, merchant, craft, gather and fishing owners to use the same authoritative capacity planner inside their transaction; do not each implement divergent stacking rules.
failures: Two grants competing for final slot -> only a valid serial result commits; no overflow bag.
Split zero, negative or more than owned -> InvalidQuantity, unchanged inventory.
Move request uses old item UUID after swap -> StaleItem, never moves the replacement.
Disconnect during drag -> no mutation unless a command committed; reconnection shows durable result.
UI refresh receives older revision -> ignore stale snapshot.
tuning: 16 slots and material MaxStack=99 are initial proposals. Optional bag expansion is a validated durable capacity change; shrinking capacity with occupied tail slots is prohibited.
observability: Record before/after container revisions and reason codes. Provide keyboard/controller move/split actions so drag/drop is not required. Large inventories use list virtualization only when measured need warrants it.

title: Equipment slots, two-hand conflicts and paper-doll visuals
purpose: Equip valid items into logical stat slots independently of sprite layer coverage. Chest and Top are one slot; Legs and Pants are one slot. A combined outfit sheet cannot be split into independent chest/leg images merely by creating gameplay slots.
fields: Slot enum: Head, Chest, Legs, Hands, Feet, Waist, Shoulders, Cloak, MainHand, OffHand, Neck, Ring1, Ring2, Trinket1, Trinket2
EquippedItemIds: map logical slot -> owned UUID; persisted and revisioned
WeaponHandPolicy: OneHand|TwoHand|OffHandOnly; shield subtype validated
VisualCoverage: stats-only|independent layer|combined outfit|missing; per definition/action/page
AppearanceRevision: replicated public snapshot, not inventory detail
EquipmentSetId and thresholds: authored stat rules; recompute once per build revision
flow: Player selects owned gear and slot; UI previews compatibility but sends item identity rather than claimed stat bonuses.
Backend validates ownership, class/level, slot type, binding and equipment state under the current session/revision.
For a two-handed weapon, plan removal of OffHand and any replaced MainHand into the bag before commit. Reject NoSpace when displaced gear cannot fit; do not delete or silently drop it.
Commit bag/equipment/binding changes and build revision together. Recompute equipment/set modifiers without accumulating duplicates.
Replicate safe visual definition IDs and appearance revision to nearby clients; owner sees full stat/item details.
