Paper-doll resolver selects compatible action-page layers. Missing shoulder/boot/glove/chest coverage displays fallback or no overlay while valid stat bonuses remain applied.
editor_steps: Create the 15-position enum and DA_EquipmentRules_Default; add aliases only at import/UI boundary, never duplicate Chest/Top or Legs/Pants slots in persistence.
Build WBP_Equipment with all logical positions and clear stats-only indicators. Two rings/trinkets have distinct slot IDs even when visually similar.
Create sword/shield/two-hand test definitions and a combined-outfit visual mapping. Add equipment component to PlayerState and appearance observer to BP_PlayerCharacter.
Reopen URPGInventoryComponent capacity planning and URPGProgressionComponent/GAS modifier rebuild to consume committed equipment changes.
Reopen DA_AnimationSet_Common and art visual matrix; explicitly record which equipped definitions replace an outfit preset, hide a layer or have no supported overlay.
failures: Equip two-hand weapon with full bag and shield equipped -> NoSpace, both current slots unchanged.
Equip shield while two-hand main weapon remains -> EquipmentConflict under initial no-auto-swap policy.
Missing visual layer -> VisualFallback warning only; stats stay active.
Sell equipped item -> reject until valid unequip or one explicitly atomic sell policy; no orphan equipment pointer.
Repeated equip/reconnect -> one modifier set and visually consistent remote avatar.
tuning: Shoulders are stats-only until art exists. Neck/rings/trinkets may remain stats-only permanently. Default equipment does not make all armor independently visible; visual compatibility is a separate production contract.
observability: Debug screen shows logical slot, UUID, definition, modifiers, active animation page and visual fallback. Screen reader labels include slot and requirements; no tiny-only drag targets.

title: Consumables, tools and item-use effects
purpose: Item use validates an owned consumable/tool and applies its authored effect under one replay-safe operation. Consuming a potion must not grant healing twice on a repeated packet, and a rejected use must not remove the item.
fields: UseDefinitionId: allowed effect, target policy, cooldown tag and consumption policy
OwnedItemReference: instance UUID or versioned stack identity
UseExecutionId/CommandId: persistent receipt for consumption; bounded live effect deduplication
ToolCategory: Pickaxe|Axe|FishingRod|CraftTool; profession requirements separate
DurabilityCost: integer policy, committed once at terminal action
UseContext: session epoch and approved target; no client-provided heal amount
flow: Player activates a hotbar item reference; server resolves actual ownership and use definition, validates target/alive state/cooldown and reserves the action.
Backend atomically consumes the stack quantity or durability and records a use entitlement/receipt with the accepted effect parameters.
Zone applies the live effect once using receipt ID and current avatar-life binding; never let a replayed receipt heal a later respawned body again.

To close a crash gap, persist the chosen consumable recovery policy: on uncertain effect application during zone crash, restore the durable post-use resource snapshot or reconcile entitlement before enabling the next avatar. Do not simply consume in SQL then forget the effect.
Publish owner inventory/resource updates and cosmetic cue from the accepted result. A non-economic gather tool check does not itself consume a tool unless the action's terminal policy says so.
On transfer, drain/reconcile item-use commands before snapshot; long cooldown expiry follows the durable cooldown policy.
editor_steps: Author DA_Item_HealingDraught with an allowed heal effect and shared item cooldown. Assign it to a versioned action-bar slot reference, not a fixed bag index.
Add URPGItemUseComponent to PlayerState/controller-authorized command route and bind WBP_ActionBar use controls.
Seed Character_A at 40/100 health with two draughts; use a proposed 30-health effect for a concrete expected result of 70 health and one remaining item.
Reopen persistence schema to include the consumable entitlement/resource-snapshot recovery rule and add crash-between-consume-and-effect fixture.
Reopen gathering/fishing/crafting tool checks to query equipment/inventory tool categories with the same item requirements; cosmetics do not establish tool ownership.
failures: Same use packet twice -> one item consumed and one 30-health application.
Potion missing or stack replaced -> ItemMissing/StaleItem, no heal.
Use while dead -> TargetInvalid before commit.
Crash after consumption before live effect -> explicit entitlement/resource recovery, not silent loss or duplicate heal.
tuning: Training potion heals 30 and uses a 10-second item cooldown; tune later. No client economy prediction. Tool durability cost is initially zero unless the terminal action definition explicitly enables it.
observability: Log receipt/effect application linkage and recovery outcomes. Hotbar tooltips show count/cooldown and keyboard/controller prompts; rejected uses have readable text.

title: Guaranteed/random loot, corpse access and replay safety
purpose: A defeated creature yields a server-created loot allocation with guaranteed entries and weighted rolls. The allocation is generated once per defeat/recipient policy; opening the corpse again never rerolls rarity or produces a second entitlement.
fields: LootAllocationId UUID; DefeatId and RecipientCharacterId unique under personal-loot policy
GuaranteedEntries: item IDs and bounded integer quantities
WeightedPools: nonnegative weights, no-drop entry optional, roll count bounded
ResolvedEntries: definition/instance IDs, rolled affixes and currency stored once
AccessPolicy: eligible personal allocation; party rule snapshotted at defeat
ClaimedEntryIds and AllocationRevision: durable; corpse Actor is only a view
ExpiryUtc: cleanup policy; unclaimed rewards do not automatically reappear
flow: Committed defeat ledger provides eligibility and loot-table version. Validate every item/family ID before enabling the encounter.
Server/backend selects each guaranteed and weighted outcome once, recording resolved entries and random audit context without exposing secret seeds to clients.
Replicate the existence/available state of the corpse and send only the eligible player their loot details. An optional visible pickup references the same allocation entry, not a second reward.
Player chooses entries; server repeats range, ownership and current allocation checks and submits one claim command.
Database transaction locks allocation and inventory, checks capacity, transfers exact entries/currency and marks them claimed with receipt/revision. NoSpace leaves unclaimed entries intact.
UI displays committed inventory result and remaining allocation. Corpse reload/reconnect queries existing allocation, never invokes generation again.
editor_steps: Create URPGLootDefinition and DA_Loot_Mossfang with guaranteed cloth scrap plus one weighted pool. Use test weights CommonMaterial=90, RareToken=9, NoDrop=1 only as a fixture.
Create BP_LootContainer with interaction interface and stable allocation reference. Enemy corpse can use it directly or spawn a view actor; choose one representation path per entry.
Build WBP_Loot with entry selection, take-all, pending/rejected states and clear ownership text.
Reopen FinalizeDefeat to create/trigger the allocation exactly once after eligible defeat commit; reopen inventory capacity service and owner snapshot observer.
Place two clients at one corpse, one eligible and one unrelated, plus a full-bag fixture. Restore the same corpse from persisted state for reload testing.
failures: Unrelated character opens personal allocation -> NotEligible; no entry details leaked.
Claim replay -> original result/AlreadyClaimed, no extra item.
Full bag -> NoSpace with allocation unchanged; currency-only claims follow explicit separate entry selection.
Missing loot item definition -> encounter content validation fails or loot quarantined with MissingLootDefinition, never substitute an arbitrary reward.
Corpse expires after UI opens -> Expired; no partial item transfer.
tuning: Personal loot is the initial simple group policy. Need/greed, master loot or shared roll UI are later rule changes requiring abuse/timeout tests. Rarity weights are content tuning, not UI constants.
observability: Audit table version, allocation, recipient, resolved item IDs and claim receipt. Track unclaimed expiry, rare-item issuance and duplicate-claim suppression.

title: Currency, merchants, stock, buyback and repairs
purpose: A merchant issues an authoritative quote, then commits currency, inventory, stock and buyback/repair changes together. Store one integer base currency; copper/silver/gold display is a conversion, not three independently editable balances.
fields: BaseCurrency bigint >=0; 100 copper=1 silver and 100 silver=1 gold display proposal
VendorId and OfferId: stable authored identifiers
QuoteId: bound to character/vendor/catalog version/price/quantity/expiry
StockState: optional finite quantity, restock generation and revision
BuybackEntryId: exact sold instance/stack, seller, paid price, expiry
RepairQuote: eligible owned item IDs, missing durability and total price
PriceModifiers: faction/reputation policy computed on authority
flow: Player talks to NPC_Mara; interaction server checks range/LOS and returns a vendor context and versioned offers.
Buy UI requests a quote for a bounded quantity. Backend/zone price rules include catalog, stock and approved reputation modifiers; client displayed total is not authority.
On confirm, lock wallet/inventory/vendor-stock/quote rows in a consistent order, repeat eligibility and capacity checks, and either apply all deltas or reject all.
Selling transfers the exact item/quantity out and creates a seller-scoped buyback entry in the same transaction that credits currency; do not reroll or recreate the sold gear.
Buyback consumes that entry and returns the same gear UUID, charging the stored price under the policy. Repairs update specific owned durability values and wallet together.
Restock uses server time and a durable generation so restart cannot multiply stock. Results update UMG from committed revisions; stale quotes are refreshed explicitly.
editor_steps: Create DA_Vendor_Mara with healing draught, starter tools, cloth and recipe offers; set one draught offer stock=1 in the contention fixture.
Create BP_NPC_Mara with NPC definition plus vendor ID; it forwards requests and never stores Character_A's wallet.
Build WBP_Merchant tabs Buy, Sell, Buyback and Repair, with quantity input, price breakdown, capacity warning and pending buttons.
Seed Character_A with 1000 base currency and Character_B with 1000, draught unit price=50 for the fixture. Configure a quote expiry and stock restock rule.
Reopen inventory/ledger/reputation consumers; use the same item identity/capacity planner for buy, sell, buyback and repair. Add a bank NPC separately but reuse interaction ownership.
failures: Two clients buy last stock -> one Purchased, one OutOfStock; only winner pays.
Insufficient funds or space -> unchanged wallet, inventory and stock.
Price changes after quote -> StaleQuote under strict quote-version policy; ask player to reconfirm.
Sell request uses replaced UUID -> StaleItem; no wrong gear sold.
Buyback after disconnect -> same original instance restored once; expired entry cannot be recovered by old UI.
Repair replay -> original receipt, no second currency charge.
tuning: Fixture prices are not a balanced economy. Proposed buyback window 2 hours, max 12 entries, quote lifetime 30 seconds. Finite stock is optional per offer; restock is not based on client clock.
observability: Track currency sources/sinks, stock contention, buyback expiry and repair spend by content version. Use int64-safe arithmetic and upper bounds; reject overflow before multiplication.

title: Bank storage and bag expansion
purpose: A bank is another owned container under the same item/stack rules, opened through a validated safe service. Moving an item between bag and bank changes location, not identity or total ownership.
fields: BankContainerId: character-owned or explicitly account-owned policy; default character-owned
BankCapacity=40 slots; bag capacity separately defined
OwnedItemId remains unchanged across storage locations
ExpectedBankRevision and InventoryRevision: stale-change checks
ExpansionEntitlementId: unique purchased unlock; new capacity bounded
BankAccessContext: banker/zone/session/range nonce
commands: MoveBankItem(CommandId, Source, Destination, ExpectedItem, Quantity) -> Moved|NoSpace|StaleItem
flow: Interact with the banker; server validates safe service and issues a bank context.
UMG displays owner-only bag and bank snapshots; a drag is only an intent with both expected revisions.
Backend locks both containers, validates ownership/binding/quantity/capacity and commits one move plus receipt.
Bank does not create a second copy of a gear instance; a uniqueness/location constraint prevents one UUID occupying two containers.
Expansion purchase debits currency and adds a unique capacity entitlement in one transaction, then publishes new slot count.
Leaving banker range or transferring closes the screen. A committed move remains durable even if its acknowledgement arrives after closure.
editor_steps: Create DA_Bank_Default and NPC_TovinBanker in Hearthford within L_Rillmere. Assign BankAccess verb and service ID.
Build WBP_Bank with paired bag/bank panels and keyboard/controller transfer controls; reuse inventory slot presentation without duplicating rules.
Seed a bank at 39/40 slots and a full variation; put a named sword UUID in bag for identity tests.
Reopen inventory service planner to support only allowlisted container types and explicit bank access. Do not expose an unrestricted MoveAnyItem endpoint.
Author one optional expansion offer with fixed capacity delta and one-time entitlement; verify persistence after zone transfer.
failures: Same UUID appears in bag and bank -> schema/transaction validation fails; quarantine inconsistent record.
Full bank withdrawal/deposit destination -> NoSpace, source remains intact.
Client calls bank command from wilderness without context -> NoAccess.
Replay expansion purchase -> same capacity and receipt, no repeated charge/unlock.
tuning: 40 bank slots and a +10 expansion are proposals. No remote anywhere-bank access initially. Account-wide banks require explicit binding and multi-character concurrency review.
observability: Audit location changes with container IDs and instance identity. Privacy: bank contents are owner-only, never replicated to nearby observers.

title: Biome resource sites, random placement and respawn
purpose: Choose resources randomly from intentionally authored eligible sites, not arbitrary map coordinates. Server selection respects biome, surface, navigation, collision, roads, quotas and active/depleted generations, and can be reproduced from recorded zone seed/cycle.
fields: ResourceSiteId: unique stable authored ID with zone, resource family and candidate transform
Eligibility: biome tags, slope limit, collision footprint, road/portal clearance, water exclusion
SpawnSeed and CycleId: server-controlled audit values; resource placement seed is not loot RNG seed
ActiveQuota and MinSpacingCm: per biome/resource category
NodeGeneration: durable per site; only current active generation can be claimed
RespawnAtUtc: committed depletion time plus approved respawn interval
WorldEpoch/ZoneInstanceId: namespace for authored/shared versus instance-local resource facts
commands: SelectActiveSites(Seed, Cycle, Quotas) -> SelectedSiteIds; server deterministic selection
flow: Content author marks candidate sites and resource tags; an Editor validator rejects duplicate IDs, unreachable positions and invalid footprint/road intersections.
On server zone startup, load durable site generations/depletion first, then choose eligible inactive candidates using the recorded seed/cycle and quotas.
Project/sweep the candidate to the intended surface, verify slope/clearance and reserve spacing; do not project to a bridge below/above accidentally without surface identity.
Spawn only approved active nodes; replicate nearby node type/generation/availability, with dormancy for unchanged nodes and explicit wake-up on depletion/respawn.
Gather completion transaction changes durable node generation state alongside reward. Director consumes the committed result and schedules respawn.
On restart, reconstruct depleted nodes/timers from backend and catch up bounded due respawns; never refill every site because the Actor was recreated.
editor_steps: Create DT_ResourceSites_Rillmere with OreSite_A01, OreSite_A02, TreeSite_W03 and an intentionally invalid road site. Store transforms in cm and surface/biome tags.
Create DA_ResourceRule_Rillmere with separate ore/tree quotas, rarity selection and spacing. Add BP_ResourceDirector once per zone with server-only authority.
Place simple graybox rock/tree meshes authored or separately licensed by the developer; no such meshes are claimed to be in the sprite ZIP.
Add footprint overlap checks and navigation/ground trace validation. Export validation diagnostics with exact rejected site ID and reason.
Reopen zone startup readiness: resource interactions remain disabled until state reconciliation finishes. Reopen node replication settings to notify late joiners of correct depleted state.
failures: Candidate sits in road, steep cliff or blocking prop -> PlacementRejected with no node.
Two directors accidentally configured -> duplicate zone owner validation fails; do not double quotas.
Server restart after depletion -> same depleted generation and due time, not a fresh grant.
Seed/cycle replay against same catalog -> same selected site set; catalog changes require new version/audit.
Backend unavailable -> no new depletion/reward operations; display degraded state, not client-side gathering fallback.
tuning: Prototype Rillmere: 12 eligible ore sites, 24 tree sites, quotas 4 ore/8 trees, minimum spacing 800 cm, road clearance 250 cm, slope <=30°. These are density test proposals; actual production catalogs are not supplied.
observability: Metrics: eligible/rejected sites by reason, active density, resource acquisition per travel minute, contention and respawn latency. Never disclose a secret loot RNG seed in public diagnostics.

title: Mining and woodcutting with exclusive claims
purpose: Mining and woodcutting share one validated action/claim pipeline but use different tool, animation, profession and yield definitions. Two clients contesting one node cannot both receive its exclusive depleted-generation reward.
fields: GatherActionId: server-generated action identity; command receipt ID stable at completion
NodeId and NodeGeneration: resolve current active source
RequiredToolCategory and MinimumProfessionLevel: authored per resource
StartPosition/StartServerTime/DurationSeconds: server action facts
ReservationOwner/Expiry: transient exclusive action lease; never itself a reward
YieldDefinitionIds, QuantityRange and ProfessionXP: server-selected content rules
CancelOnMove/Hit/Death/Travel/ToolChange: explicit flags
flow: Character_A and Character_B press Interact on OreSite_A01. Server checks range/LOS, active generation, pickaxe ownership, mining skill and action state.
The zone serializes reservation acquisition: A wins; B receives ResourceBusy and no materials/XP. Reservations expire/cancel safely if A moves away.
Server advances a 3-second mining action. The p2 tool pose is cosmetic; a missing/late hit-frame notify cannot finish the action or award ore.

At completion repeat tool/range/alive/generation checks and capacity plan. Backend transaction locks node generation and character, marks depleted, grants resolved ore plus mining XP and stores receipt atomically.
After commit replicate node depletion to both clients, update A's inventory/profession UI, and schedule persisted respawn. B's subsequent request receives NodeDepleted.
For TreeSite_W03 repeat with Axe, woodcutting profession, biome-specific AshLog yields and chopping visual mapping. Invalid terrain sites are never spawned.
On timeout after commit, quarantine that action/node from conflicting mutations and reconcile the original receipt. Restart reads depleted state; no second grant.
editor_steps: Create DA_GatherRule_Mining and DA_GatherRule_Woodcutting with tool tags, durations, yield tables and profession IDs. Add corresponding material definitions created in Phase 09.
Add URPGGatheringComponent once to BP_PlayerCharacter and expose RequestGather/CancelGather as guarded custom commands.
Configure BP_ResourceNode with source identity, resource definition and interaction interface; it does not own a copy of player inventory.
Assign WBP_Gathering to ScreenRouter's nonmodal progress layer. Show target, progress, cancel prompt and structured rejection; input remains responsive but movement cancels under default rule.

Reopen resource director to consume committed depletion, inventory service to plan yield capacity, profession component to apply receipt XP, and PaperZD mappings for mining/chopping p2 only after actual archive audit.
Test both clients against one node, one full inventory, one missing tool, one moving player and a backend response dropped after commit.
failures: Two simultaneous starts -> one reservation; one ResourceBusy.
A cancels/moves/dies -> reservation released, no materials/XP; B can start if node remains active.
Completion races with stale generation -> NodeDepleted/StaleGeneration, no grant.
Full bag -> NoSpace before depletion commit; node stays active and reservation releases.
Server restart after accepted depletion -> ore/log remains granted once; respawn uses stored due time.
Repeated bot-like requests -> rate limited without issuing duplicate actions; avoid punishing packet retries as new activity.
tuning: Mining duration 3 s, woodcutting 4 s, yield 2 CopperOre or 3 AshLog, profession XP 5, respawn 180 s are fixture proposals. Optional herbalism may reuse this path only after its content/art/tool policy is approved.
observability: Log node/site/generation/action/character/receipt and cancellation reason. Progress has text and audio-optional cues; tool animation is not the only indication. Track acquisition rate and contention for economy tuning.

title: Recipes, professions, stations and deterministic results
purpose: Crafting consumes a validated recipe's resources and produces deterministic output in one durable operation. Blacksmithing, Alchemy, Cooking and Tailoring start as templates with separate profession progression and learned recipe sets.
fields: RecipeId and Version: stable recipe.* ID; ingredients/result from server catalog
IngredientRequirements: definition IDs, integer quantities and allowed substitutes only if authored
RequiredProfessionId/Level and LearnedRecipeEntitlement: durable
StationTag/ToolTag and RangeCm: validation, not merely UI decoration
CurrencyCost and BatchLimit: bounded integers
ResultDefinitionId/Quantity and FixedAffixes: deterministic initial policy
CraftActionId/CommandId: terminal receipt generates stable output instance identity
commands: RequestCraft(CommandId, RecipeId, BatchCount, StationContext, ExpectedInventoryRevision) -> Started|MissingMaterials|RecipeLocked
flow: At Station_Forge the player selects IronHatchet. UI previews 4 CopperOre, 2 AshLog and 25 currency, required Blacksmithing level 1 and deterministic one-hatchet output.
Server verifies interaction, learned recipe, profession/tool/station gates, batch bound and alive/action state; it starts the authored craft duration without consuming materials yet.
On completion revalidate current ingredients and output capacity using one planned transaction, including space freed by consumed stacks.
Backend locks character inventory/wallet/profession/recipe records, consumes exact materials/currency, creates one gear UUID, adds profession XP and receipt together.
Return committed output identity and revisions. PaperZD/tool/VFX cues observe success; no animation notify calls material consumption or output grant.

Disconnect immediately after confirm or commit: unresolved action cancels under policy, but committed receipt remains. On another zone login, load the one hatchet and consumed inputs without replaying the recipe.
Repeat-craft requests use separate bounded commands after prior receipt or an explicitly atomic batch; never an unbounded client loop.
editor_steps: Create four profession definitions and station tags: Forge/Blacksmithing, AlchemyBench/Alchemy, Cookfire/Cooking, Loom/Tailoring.

Author DA_Recipe_IronHatchet, DA_Recipe_HealingDraught, DA_Recipe_GrilledDace and DA_Recipe_WovenCloak with fixed outputs. Cooking input can come from the development fixture/vendor before fishing Phase 14; replace that sourcing path in the integrated loop afterward.
Place BP_CraftingStation at Hearthford forge with StationId and tag; attach interaction interface only, not character inventory.
Build WBP_Crafting with recipe filters, learned/locked state, ingredient counts, result tooltip, quantity and confirm/cancel. Bind counts to current inventory revision.
Reopen gathering/loot/vendor catalogs so each ingredient has a real source. Add native component to authorized player command route and connect backend atomic command endpoint.
Create delayed-after-commit and disconnect-before-completion service fixtures; rejoin L_Thornweald to verify exactly-one output.
failures: Missing materials/profession/recipe -> explicit reason, no consumption.
Two crafts compete for same ore -> only valid serialized outcome commits; no negative materials.
Output does not fit after planned consumption -> NoSpace and no input/currency loss.
Disconnect after commit -> one output on reconnect; retry returns same UUID.
Unknown recipe version -> StaleRecipe; require refreshed preview/confirmation.
Batch=0, negative or over limit -> InvalidQuantity; no loop or overflow.
tuning: IronHatchet example costs/yield and 4-second craft duration are tuning proposals. Initial success is deterministic; quality/failure rolls are disabled until audit/balance rules are approved.
observability: Ledger links recipe version, consumed stacks, output UUID and profession XP. Craft UI supports controller quantity changes and text ingredient deficits. Track material sinks, output volume and disconnect reconciliation.

title: Water casts, bobber, bite, reel and catch transaction
purpose: Fishing is a server-owned timed attempt at an eligible water region. The rod overlay and bobber visualize casting/waiting/bite/reel states; neither a notify nor a delayed packet can create a second catch.
fields: FishingAttemptId UUID; CharacterId/session epoch; WaterBodyId and pool version
CastPointCm: finite bounded point inside approved water polygon/volume
BobberPosition: accepted world-space point, not attached to screen or character
BiteStartServerSeconds and BiteEndServerSeconds: server timing, secret until relevant cue
ReelSequenceId: one accepted reaction per attempt
ResolvedSpeciesId/Quantity/ProfessionXP: stored terminal result, not rerolled on UI open
TerminalState: Caught|Failed|Canceled; one terminal receipt per attempt
flow: Player equips/owns a FishingRod and aims from reachable shoreline. Server verifies water ID, pool, range, LOS, dry/shore policy and action state.
Create one attempt and accepted cast point; replicate cosmetic cast/bobber state. p3 rod poses must match body/outfit pages after actual source inspection.
Server chooses an auditable wait/bite schedule and opens the reaction window on its own clock; clients show cues using replicated accepted times.

Player reels. Server validates the active attempt, current actor/session, one unused input sequence and receipt time within the allowed reaction policy; client claimed timestamps are not blindly trusted.

On success select species from the approved biome pool and enabled weather/time modifiers, then atomically store terminal result, grant fish/profession XP and applicable rod durability cost with inventory capacity checks.
UI/audio play from committed result and destroy the bobber. Late notifies/reel packets return AlreadyResolved and cannot grant fish.

Disconnect/restart before terminal commit cancels unresolved attempt under lease-recovery policy; committed catch remains in inventory on reconnect. Never resume an old bite window into a new session.
editor_steps: Create BP_WaterRegion with Water_Rill, surface bounds and DA_FishingPool_Rillmere. Mark a reachable ShoreSpot_A and validate cast-point traces against real water/terrain.
Create BP_FishingBobber as a nonauthoritative visual representation of accepted attempt/point, with one owner/action association and explicit teardown.
Create DA_FishingPool_Rillmere with RiverDace/Mudfin weights and a small no-catch/failure policy; species are item definitions with separate text/icons/art tasks.
Add URPGFishingComponent and WBP_Fishing progress/reaction UI. Use IA_Primary/IA_FishReel or an explicit context mapping, not a second global click handler that also attacks.
Reopen item tool validation, inventory/profession transaction, water/swimming cancellation and PaperZD action mapping. Missing p3 clothing uses a declared compatible fallback.
Run replay, early/late reel, full-bag, movement-cancel, rod-swap, disconnect and server-restart fixtures with Client_B observing the bobber but not private loot details.
failures: Reel before bite -> TooEarly under chosen fail-or-continue policy; no fish.
Late/replayed reel after Caught -> AlreadyResolved, unchanged inventory.
Full bag at terminal commit -> NoSpace, no fish or profession XP; attempt fails terminally rather than waiting indefinitely for a free slot.
Move/swim/unequip rod -> Canceled; bobber removed on all relevant clients.
Server dies during Waiting/BiteWindow -> unresolved attempt canceled on recovery; no automatic catch.
Commit acknowledgement lost -> receipt restores original fish once, even in another zone.
tuning: Proposed cast range 1200 cm, wait 3–8 s, reaction window 1.5 s, one fish and 5 fishing XP. Accessibility can offer longer authored reaction windows consistently validated server-side; no client-only timing advantage.
observability: Track attempt transitions, server reaction latency, terminal result and pool version. Bite cue uses text/visual/audio, with audio optional. Weather/time modifiers are disabled until shared world-state versioning is implemented.

title: NPC roles, branching dialogue and consequence records
purpose: One NPC may offer dialogue, quests, merchant, trainer and crafting services without duplicating player state. Conditions and choices are authored; lasting consequences are validated character records, not booleans hidden in a widget.
fields: NPCDefinitionId: name/localization key, role/service IDs, faction and visual set
DialogueId/NodeId/OptionId: stable IDs, versioned graph
ConditionSet: quest state, reputation threshold, class/profession, flags; read-only evaluation
ChoiceConsequenceId: unique authored operation with repeat/idempotency policy
ConversationNonce: character/NPC/zone/epoch binding and expiry
Text: localization keys and arguments, not hardcoded sentence concatenation
flow: Player interacts within range/LOS; server resolves NPC roles and current condition facts, returning only available choices and a conversation nonce.
UMG shows localized text/options and stores no authoritative quest/reputation variables.
Player chooses an option ID; server re-evaluates conditions and node/nonce/version, since another action may have changed quest state.
Pure conversation advances without an economic write; a lasting choice uses an idempotent backend command for consequence flags/reputation/reward as defined.
Merchant/trainer/quest/craft option opens the relevant service context; that domain repeats validation for its eventual commit.
Leaving range, NPC despawn, death or travel closes conversation, unbinds UI and invalidates nonce. Late replies from old zone generations are ignored.
editor_steps: Create URPGNPCDefinition and URPGDialogueDefinition schemas. Author NPC_Mara as quartermaster/quest giver/vendor and NPC_Tovin as banker/trainer contact with separate service IDs.
Build DA_Dialogue_Mara with greeting, missing-supplies quest offer, in-progress reminder, ready-to-complete and completed nodes; include an optional reputation-sensitive branch.
Create BP_NPC_Mara from ARPGServiceNPC with interaction and sprite presentation but no hostile AI requirement. Static and animated NPCs share service ownership rules.
Build WBP_Dialogue with speaker name, text, option list, close and focus restoration; options are keyed by ID rather than array index alone.
Reopen quest/vendor/trainer components to accept an NPC context and return explicit eligibility reasons; never copy quest inventory into the NPC actor.
failures: Choice condition changed after screen opened -> ConditionChanged and refreshed node; no unauthorized reward.
Option ID from another dialogue -> InvalidOption.
NPC disappears mid-command -> reversible conversation closes; committed consequence remains and receipt resolves.
Duplicate choice reward packet -> original receipt/AlreadyApplied.
Locale changes with long text -> layout remains usable and choices reachable.
tuning: No voiced dialogue requirement initially. Optional persistent choices should not irreversibly block main progression; provide alternate routes. Day/night schedules are a later world-life feature with service availability fallback.
observability: Audit consequence ID/quest state and reason codes, not unnecessary full dialogue transcripts. Text supports subtitles, scaling, controller navigation and localization keys.

title: Quest DAG, objectives, journal and once-only rewards
purpose: Quests track server-approved actions through a versioned dependency graph. The journal is an observer. Gathering, combat, loot, delivery, talk, interaction, exploration, crafting, fishing and dungeon/boss objectives each consume explicit verified events.
fields: QuestId/version and prerequisite quest DAG: no cycles
ObjectiveId/type/target/count: stable IDs; types Kill,Gather,Loot,Deliver,Talk,Interact,Explore,Craft,Fish,DungeonBoss
QuestState and objective counters: durable, monotonic under objective policy
EventId: unique verified gameplay fact; objective-event deduplication
RewardEntitlementId: unique character/quest/completion-cycle key
RepeatPolicy: None initially; explicit server cycle ID for future repeatables/dailies
PartySharePolicy: per objective, not blanket nearby-player credit
commands: AbandonQuest(CommandId, QuestId) -> Abandoned|CannotAbandon; declared item cleanup
flow: NPC_Mara offers RoadSupplies only when prerequisites/level/flags permit; Accept persists active state and zeroed objective identities.
Player kills a Mossfang, loots cloth, mines CopperOre, chops AshLog, catches RiverDace and crafts IronHatchet. Each domain emits a verified, deduplicated gameplay fact after its authoritative commit.
Quest component/backend applies matching objective progress once using EventId; an item purchase cannot masquerade as a Gather event unless the objective intentionally asks for possession.
Delivery checks current owned items at turn-in and consumes them atomically; prior gather progress is not proof the materials are still owned.
When objectives are complete, dialogue/journal show ready state. Claim validates NPC/range, current objective state, reward choice and inventory capacity.
One transaction consumes delivery items, records completion/consequences, grants XP/currency/item, unlocks the next quest and stores reward receipt. Cross-zone retry returns the existing result.
Abandonment follows authored cleanup without rerolling/regranting rewards on reacceptance. Repeatables require explicit cycle IDs and are not enabled by default.
editor_steps: Create DA_Quest_RoadSupplies and a small chain: FirstSteps -> RoadSupplies -> TheSluiceSignal. Validate prerequisite DAG, stable objective IDs and reward references.
Build WBP_QuestJournal and WBP_ObjectiveTracker with available/active/ready/completed states, pin/unpin and map marker links. Do not use widget booleans as quest state.

Add URPGQuestComponent to PlayerState and subscribe to verified fact receipts emitted by prior combat/gather/fish/craft/loot/explore systems. Backfill is opt-in per objective, not accidental replay of all historical events.
Reopen DA_Dialogue_Mara to branch on authoritative quest state and offer turn-in. Add quest-giver/ready markers to NPC presentation using safe public or owner-only state.

Seed exact objective counts in the worked chain and add a full-bag turn-in fixture. Include separate objective samples for talk/interact/explore/deliver/dungeon so every supported type has a test row.
failures: Replay gather/kill EventId -> unchanged objective count.
Purchase ore for a Gather objective -> no progress; possession/delivery objectives behave separately.
Full bag at final reward -> NoSpace, delivery items not consumed, quest remains ready.
Claim after zone transfer with old nonce -> refreshed NPC context required; completed entitlement cannot grant twice.
Quest DAG cycle or missing target -> content validation failure.
Abandon/reaccept after completed reward -> no new entitlement for a nonrepeatable quest.
tuning: RoadSupplies fixture requires 1 kill, 1 loot, 2 ore, 3 logs, 1 fish and 1 craft; rewards proposed 100 XP and 200 currency. Escort quests are gated until navigation/recovery/party proof; daily resets are not approved/enabled.
observability: Track QuestId/ObjectiveId/EventId and reward receipt, not client tracker animations. Objective text has pluralization/localization support and clear source verbs; map markers do not expose undiscovered secrets unintentionally.

title: Four classes, talents, prerequisites and respec
purpose: Vanguard, Ranger, Arcanist and Warden share a common body but differ through authored abilities, stat growth and talent graphs. The backend validates points, prerequisites/exclusivity and respec atomically; UI lines on a tree are not rules.
fields: ClassId: stable class.* ID; common BodyId
SkillTreeId/Version and NodeId: stable graph identities
PrerequisiteNodeIds, MinimumLevel, PointCost and MaxRank: bounded authored constraints
ExclusiveGroupId: mutually exclusive branches where designed
UnlockedAbilityIds/PassiveEffectIds: resolved from purchased node/rank
SpentPoints and EarnedPoints: validated totals, never negative
RespecQuoteId/Cost and BuildRevision: server-calculated
flow: Player opens WBP_Skills and sees eligible nodes computed from the current versioned build; locked nodes explain exact missing requirements.
Spend request identifies node/rank only. Server/backend checks class, level, points, prerequisites, exclusive group and current build revision.
Commit node ranks and point spend, increment build revision, and return the new durable build.
Zone rebuilds GAS granted abilities/passives from the committed set, removing obsolete grants/effects without duplicating remaining ones.

At trainer, respec quote specifies cost and scope; confirmation debits currency and resets the selected tree/ranks in one transaction. Restore required baseline abilities independent of optional talent choices.
Reconnect/transfer reconstructs the same build from stable IDs; content migration validates removed/replaced nodes and refunds points under a recorded policy.
editor_steps: Author four DA_Class_* growth/ability catalogs and four DA_SkillTree_* graphs. Start Vanguard/Ranger combat visuals in the slice when supported; Arcanist/Warden casting/healing visuals are explicit art tasks.
Populate sources/class-catalog.json with six example abilities and a small three-branch talent plan per class; these are production templates, not a balanced 50-level tree.
Build WBP_Skills with keyboard/controller node navigation, rank/cost/requirements, confirmation and respec preview. Use a list alternative for accessibility.
Place NPC_TovinTrainer and assign trainer service plus class/profession offers. Reopen dialogue, wallet and GAS grant lifecycle for the respec result.
Validate graph acyclicity, class membership, no required story gate tied to an irrevocable exclusive node, and all referenced ability/effect IDs.
failures: Spend same points concurrently -> one valid commit; other StaleRevision/InsufficientPoints.
Skip prerequisite via forged request -> PrerequisiteMissing.
Buy both exclusive branches -> ExclusiveConflict.
Disconnect after respec charge -> one reset/charge, correct build on reconnect.
Patch removes node -> migration/refund record, no silent loss or unplayable character.
tuning: Proposed one talent point per level after level 1, cap 50, starter respec cost 500 base currency. Costs/growth/branches are tuning proposals. No permanent class race/body art claim.
observability: Audit build revision, node rank deltas, respec receipt and stat rebuild. Tooltips disclose active/passive effects and prerequisites without hidden UI-only conditions.

title: World map, minimap, markers and discovery
purpose: A map presents authored geography and server-approved discovery. Minimap position is local presentation of approved movement; hidden quest/resource details are not indiscriminately replicated to every client.
fields: RegionId/LandmarkId/MarkerId: stable IDs and zone-local transforms
MapProjection: world X/Y bounds to normalized map coordinates; Z layers explicit for interiors
DiscoveredRegionIds and UnlockedHubIds: durable character facts
MarkerVisibilityPolicy: Public|Discovered|QuestOwner|Party|Hidden
MapTexture/VectorLayout: separate authored art, not supplied by sprite archive
SelectedWaypoint: local preference; navigation is advisory, not teleport authority
commands: RequestFastTravelFromMarker(HubId) -> TravelRequest; delegates to validated travel service
flow: Server verifies the capsule entered a registered discovery volume on a valid surface and emits a stable discovery event.
Backend adds the region/landmark unlock once, returns revision and any deliberately authored reward entitlement.
UI overlays discovered regions, quest-owner markers, party markers and current approved location using the zone map transform.
Interior/bridge layers use explicit floor/layer IDs; do not pretend a flat sprite map automatically describes every 3D height.
Selecting a marker shows route/zone destination and services; only unlocked safe hubs expose fast-travel requests.
On zone handoff switch map catalog after destination readiness; clear old actor markers and retain durable discoveries.
editor_steps: Create DA_Map_Rillmere with world bounds, layers and marker catalog. Add BP_DiscoveryVolume at OldSluice and west road regions.
Build WBP_Map and WBP_Minimap with icons plus text labels/legend, zoom/pan and controller focus; minimap rotation remains fixed to the camera/world convention.
Reopen quest/NPC/gate definitions to assign marker IDs and visibility policy, not hardcoded widget coordinates.
Author a simple rights-cleared graybox map diagram until proper map art is produced. Register its source/provenance separately.
Test every zone entrance against the map transform and validate reciprocal gate destinations.
failures: Client requests discovery without being in volume -> reject; no unlock.
Duplicate entry/reconnect -> one discovery record/reward.
Quest marker from old zone arrives late -> ignored by zone generation.
Minimap maps bridge to wrong layer -> content validation/QA failure, not navigation teleport.
tuning: Proposed landmark spacing 2–4 minutes walking and map reveal by authored regions rather than per-pixel fog. These are content pacing targets, not measured world scale.
observability: Log discovery event IDs and map transform errors. Markers have labels/shapes and adjustable scale; important paths are not color-only.

title: Shared time, lighting, weather and biome modifiers
purpose: Replicate a shared server clock epoch and weather state, then let clients render lighting and transitions locally. Fishing/resource modifiers read the authoritative weather/time version, not a client sky material.
fields: WorldTimeEpochUtc and GameDaySeconds: durable configuration; server time offset replicated
WeatherStateId, TransitionStart/EndServerSeconds and WeatherRevision
BiomeWeatherWeights: authored finite nonnegative values and allowed transitions
GameplayModifiersEnabled=false until tested
LightingCurveIds: sun intensity/color/fog parameters as cosmetic authoring
ScheduleTimeBucket: coarse shared clock view for later NPC schedules
commands: SelectWeather(ZoneId, CycleId) -> WeatherTransition; server seeded policy
flow: Zone initializes world epoch/cycle policy from backend/world configuration and publishes a compact synchronized time snapshot.
Server selects a permitted biome weather transition and increments revision; clients interpolate light/fog/rain from accepted start/end.
Gameplay action captures the relevant time/weather revision at its declared sampling point. Fishing pool modifiers do not change mid-transaction because a local rain effect loaded late.
Late joiner receives current state and transition times, not a multicast history replay.
Server restart resumes the persisted/derived cycle policy without multiple immediate weather events or reset exploits.
NPC schedules may later consume time buckets, but core vendors remain recoverably accessible and no ecosystem simulation is required.
editor_steps: Create DA_Weather_Rillmere with Clear/Overcast/Rain transitions and a day-light curve. Place BP_WorldClock once in each zone; authority publishes state through GameState/component.
Create local lighting/weather presentation components with capped Niagara/emitter counts and scalability options. Keep weather visuals off dedicated-server render paths.
Bind WBP_HUD to weather/time text/icon cues. Reopen fishing/resource definitions only when enabling specific modifiers with a versioned rule.
Test midday/night, transition join, low effects setting and server restart using accelerated development clock values.
Record real-world UTC versus game-time semantics in save schema; do not persist a different clock in each player SaveGame.
failures: Client changes system clock -> no gameplay yield change.
Late join during storm -> same state/time interpolation, not clear until next event.
Weather definition missing -> safe Clear fallback for presentation and disable gameplay modifier with diagnostic.
Restart during transition -> consistent resumed/derived state, no repeated world-event reward.
tuning: Proposed 60-minute game day, 10–20-minute weather dwell and no gameplay modifiers initially. Lighting/performance/readability must be tested on actual sprite materials.
observability: Record clock offset error and weather revision, not per-frame sky values. Provide reduced weather particles/flashes and clear storm warnings without relying solely on sound.

title: Biome production, navigation, density and interiors
purpose: Create new authored zones through catalogs, reusable Blueprint actors and content validation instead of changing C++ for every forest or town. Six region designs define a long-term world plan; they are not six finished 3D maps.
fields: ZoneDefinitionId, MapSoftPath, ContentVersion and allowed entrance IDs
BiomeTags, climate/light/weather definitions and level range
PopulationBudget: enemy/resource/NPC/prop density and active actor caps
NavigationSurfacePolicy: walkable slopes, stairs, bridges, water and interiors
TravelTimeTargetsSeconds: authored route targets, measured in test runs
RequiredAssetProvenance: mesh/material/audio/sprite licenses and source references
commands: MeasureRoute(RouteId) -> TravelTimeSamples; QA procedure, not a fabricated benchmark
flow: Start from the zone brief and adjacency graph; choose entrances and service placement before detailed art.
Graybox landscape/roads/interiors with developer-owned simple meshes and scale markers; build collision/navigation and test capsule traversal.
Register map/entrances/resources/water/NPC/encounter/quest/map-marker definitions with stable IDs. Run content validation and fix every missing reference.
Add small encounter/resource populations, place service hub and one end-to-end quest route, then run two clients and transfer/reconnect tests.
Measure travel times, navigation failures, resource/encounter density and client/server budgets. Only then replace graybox art and consider internal streaming.
Package/cook the exact map references and content version; allocation refuses a server with mismatched catalogs. Expand in measured batches rather than claiming an endless world.
editor_steps: Use File > New Level and the appropriate simple/open-world template after checking installed 5.8.3 behavior; start simple for the slice. Save to the registered Content/Game/Maps path.

Author Landscape or modular 3D geometry, collision, PlayerStarts, NavMesh bounds, water regions, gate actors and safe hub. Use named folders in World Outliner for services/encounters/resources/entrances.
Create the zone Data Asset and tables; register with URPGZoneCatalog and the backend zone allocator. Reopen neighboring gates for reciprocal destinations.
Add minimap bounds, audio zones, climate definition, quest links and telemetry IDs. Keep routine content editable through Blueprint/Data Assets.
Test interior entry/exit, bridge layers, slopes, swim shores, resource placement rejection and remote sprites before dressing with vegetation/buildings.
failures: Missing return gate or invalid entrance -> catalog validation fails; zone not allocatable.
No navmesh on required route -> blocked production gate.
Resource quota places nodes in road -> reject candidate, not overlap buildings.
Map soft reference omitted from cook -> packaged admission fails in test; fix asset manager/cook inclusion before release.
tuning: Initial density/travel targets are in each zone brief and must be replaced by measured values. World Partition is optional internal streaming, not a backend zone-server router. No supplied 3D meshes are assumed.
observability: Content QA records route times, stuck locations, density, draw/actor budgets and provenance. Provide readable landmarks and alternative route signage; avoid inaccessible mandatory jump sequences.

title: Parties, invitations, group credit and leadership
purpose: A minimal party/eligibility contract is needed before group combat rewards; full invite/leave/leader UI arrives in Phase 19. Party membership is a versioned social record, not a list invented independently by each zone server.
fields: PartyId UUID; PartyRevision bigint; leader CharacterId
MemberCharacterIds and roles: bounded unique membership
InviteId, inviter/invitee, expiry and acceptance state
MaxMembers=4 initially; dungeon eligibility uses the same policy
CreditSnapshot: member IDs/revision at verified encounter event
CrossZonePresence: backend/social routing projection, not direct Actor references
flow: Phase 08 uses a service-created Party_AB fixture with two authenticated members; no public invitation UI is required for Slice A.
In Phase 19 inviter selects an identity, server/backend validates block/membership/capacity and stores a short-lived invitation.
Invitee accepts using their own authenticated session; backend atomically updates party membership/revision and invitation state.
Zone servers receive safe membership/presence projections; party UI binds by CharacterId and resolves currently relevant actor pointers transiently.
Combat/quest/dungeon systems snapshot eligible party members under their own proximity/contribution/share policies; joining after defeat does not retroactively obtain loot.
Leave/disband/leader disconnect follows deterministic succession policy and invalidates stale pending instance reservations as required.
editor_steps: Create PartyPolicy and DB_party_memberships/DB_party_memberships/DB_party_memberships records before group rewards. Seed Party_AB in the development service at Phase 08.
Create WBP_Party with name/class/health/presence indicators, invite response, leave and leader controls; advanced UI integration is explicitly Phase 19.
Reopen encounter and quest rules to use membership revision plus deliberate eligibility, not all nearby actors.
Reopen dungeon allocator to reserve a coherent party roster, and chat routing to use authenticated party membership.
Test cross-zone presence and one disconnected member without leaking private inventory or making a stale Actor pointer authoritative.
failures: Two invitations accepted into different parties concurrently -> membership uniqueness allows one valid result.
Party fills before accept -> PartyFull.
Blocked player invites -> Blocked with privacy-safe response.
Leader disconnects -> declared succession after grace, not a permanently unusable party.
Member joins after kill -> no retroactive defeat reward.
tuning: Four members and a 60-second invitation TTL are proposals. Initial equal XP split applies only to eligible members; quests explicitly declare shared versus personal objectives.
observability: Audit membership revisions and invitation results. Party UI supports keyboard/controller navigation and clear disconnected/out-of-zone status.

title: Elite phases, boss telegraphs and instanced dungeons
purpose: A small co-op dungeon is an independently allocated zone instance with a declared party roster, encounter state and recovery policy. Boss phases and telegraphs are server decisions; matching does not appear automatically because a dedicated server exists.
fields: DungeonDefinitionId and InstanceId; max party size and level/quest gates
ReservationRoster and PartyRevision: immutable admission snapshot or explicit update
EncounterState/PhaseId/PhaseRevision: server-owned, persisted at chosen checkpoints
TelegraphSpec: shape/radius/direction/start/end and safe areas
BossDefeatId and per-character reward entitlement: unique per instance/encounter generation
InstanceExpiry/CheckpointId: recovery policy; lockouts disabled initially
flow: Party leader requests SluiceVault; backend validates roster/revision, requirements and available instance capacity and reserves a server.
Each member receives their own identity-bound transfer ticket; one player failure does not cause whole-server travel of unrelated players.
Instance initializes registered encounters and checkpoint. Boss health thresholds/time rules select phases and publish telegraph state before impact.
Server validates all melee/projectile/area hits; telegraph graphics cannot cause damage, and low visual settings must retain gameplay-critical shape cues.
Boss defeat creates a unique durable encounter/reward receipt and completion fact for quests; loot rights use the declared party eligibility snapshot.
Reconnect returns to an active reserved instance when valid. Server crash recovers from durable checkpoint under a documented reset policy with existing reward entitlements preserved.
editor_steps: Author DA_Dungeon_SluiceVault with entrance/exit IDs, four-member limit, checkpoint and boss definitions. Create L_SluiceVault as a graybox interior with navigation and camera-occlusion tests.
Create DA_Enemy_SluiceKeeper with two phases: cone sweep then alternating water-lane area effects; all art/meshes/VFX are acquisition/authoring tasks.
Place BP_DungeonController and encounter spawners; connect their state to the backend instance record and zone transfer system.
Build WBP_DungeonFinder with party readiness, requirements, queue/reservation status and cancel. Start a simple explicit party-entry queue before automated role matching.
Reopen party/quest/loot/recovery components to handle instance identity and reconnect; test wipe/reset after one already-rewarded encounter.
failures: Party roster changes after reservation -> require refresh or explicit allowed member update; no unauthorized entrant.
Boss threshold processed twice -> one phase transition/cue sequence.
Server restart after boss reward -> no second loot/quest completion.
Player disconnects during telegraph -> server simulation continues; rejoin obeys safe checkpoint policy.
Instance expired -> return to safe hub with preserved durable inventory/quests.
tuning: First dungeon target 15–25 minutes for four players is a proposal; start with one boss and two encounter rooms. No raids, global matchmaking service or mass concurrency claim.
observability: Record queue/reservation/transfer latency, encounter phase, wipes, reward receipts and checkpoint recovery. Telegraphs include shape/time cues and reduced-flash variants.

title: Zone/local/party chat, private messages and moderation
purpose: Chat routes authenticated messages to deliberate audiences and enforces limits, blocks and moderation. Local/zone chat is not an unrestricted reliable multicast from any client; private messages and reports require identity-aware routing.
fields: MessageId UUID; SenderCharacterId server-resolved; channel ID
Channel: Local|Zone|Party|Private|Guild when guilds exist
Text: bounded Unicode, normalized for control-character/abuse policy; not executable rich markup
Audience: distance/zone/party/guild/block policy resolved by authority
RateLimitState and MuteExpiryUtc: server/backend moderation state
ReportId: reporter, message reference, reason and retention policy; no public credentials
commands: BlockOrReportMessage(MessageId, Reason) -> Recorded|NotFound; authenticated social service
flow: Client composes in WBP_Chat; entering text suspends conflicting gameplay key bindings locally but does not pause the server.
Server resolves sender identity and validates channel membership, message length, rate limit, mute/block and recipient policy.
Route local messages to eligible nearby clients, zone messages within the instance, party/guild messages via social membership and private messages via identity routing.
Store only the moderation/audit retention selected for that channel; delivered chat is rendered as text, not evaluated HTML/commands.
Reports reference message IDs and authorized moderation tools record action/reason/auditor. Blocks take effect across invites/private chat and relevant social interactions.
On reconnect restore social restrictions; do not resend locally queued old messages automatically as new chat.
editor_steps: Create DA_ChatPolicy_Default with channel permissions, maximum length and rate limits. Add URPGChatComponent to the authenticated controller/social route.
Build WBP_Chat with channel selector, history, compose, mute/report/block controls and visible send failures. Use text widgets rather than unsanitized rich markup.
Configure zone/local audience resolution and backend party/private routing; no separate message-bus cluster is required for the first deployment.
Create MutedAccountFixture, BlockedPairFixture and flood fixture; reopen party/guild/friends interfaces for membership checks.
Define a moderation runbook, accessible reporting flow and data retention/appeal policy before public access. Exact legal obligations require separate jurisdiction review.
failures: Forged sender name/ID -> server identity replaces/rejects it.
Flood/replayed send -> bounded RateLimited/duplicate result, not server reliable queue exhaustion.
Blocked private message -> not delivered; privacy-safe sender result.
Muted account reconnects -> mute remains enforced.
Markup/control characters -> safe text/rejection, no UI injection.
tuning: Proposed 300 Unicode characters and 5 messages per 10 seconds with burst limit 3; tune moderation/accessibility and localization needs. Do not rely on keyword filters as complete moderation.
observability: Metrics count channel volume/rejections/reports without logging credentials. Screen-reader announcements are configurable to avoid flooding; chat text size is adjustable.

title: Friends, presence, blocking and account recovery
purpose: Friends and block lists are durable identity relationships. Presence is an authorized projection, not a durable promise that a particular actor remains loaded. Account recovery belongs to the authentication provider/service, not an NPC or local save edit.
fields: RelationshipOwnerId and TargetIdentityId: explicit account/character scope; default account-level privacy with character display
FriendRequestId/state/expiry; bilateral accepted relationship
BlockRecord: owner/target; precedence over private messages/invites/trade
Presence: Online|Away|Offline plus privacy-approved zone detail
RecoveryProviderId: configured account recovery route, no password stored by game UI
flow: Player finds a character through a bounded name/identity lookup; server applies privacy and rate limits without exposing account secrets.
Friend request records are authenticated and deduplicated; acceptance creates the authorized bilateral relationship.
Block writes take precedence and immediately invalidate delivery/invite/trade eligibility according to policy.
Presence combines active session leases and user privacy settings; it expires when a lease ends rather than persisting a stale Online flag.
WBP_Social updates from service results and local notifications; actor references are resolved only for currently relevant in-zone players.
Recovery opens the configured provider flow; after identity is regained, load the same durable account/characters through normal validation.
editor_steps: Define account-versus-character relationship semantics in DA_SocialPolicy_Default; do not mix them opportunistically across features.
Create DB_social_edges, DB_social_edges and DB_social_edges with uniqueness constraints and deletion/retention policy.
Build WBP_Social with requests, friends, blocked list, private-message and invite controls; blocked actions are clearly disabled.
Reopen chat/party/trade to consult the same block policy rather than copied lists. Add account recovery link to WBP_Login, not a game-side password reset implementation.
Test cross-zone presence and logout lease expiry with two accounts.
failures: Duplicate request -> one request, no notification spam.
Blocked target gets invite/trade/private message -> denied by common policy.
Presence cache stale after crash -> expires; no secret zone/online disclosure beyond privacy policy.
Recover wrong provider account -> cannot access another AccountId's characters.
tuning: Proposed friend limit 100 and request TTL 7 days; retain only needed data. No public friend graph or exact location sharing by default.
observability: Audit relationship changes and abuse-rate counters with privacy controls. Social lists support text search, keyboard navigation and localized presence states.

title: Consensual player trading and escrow
purpose: A secure trade binds both players' acceptances to one immutable offer revision and commits both inventories/currencies together. Never implement trade as one player sending an item followed by a separate payment.
fields: TradeId UUID; ParticipantA/B CharacterIds; current OfferRevision
OfferItems: exact UUIDs/versioned stacks/quantities and currency integers
AcceptanceA/B: revision-specific; editing clears both acceptances
EscrowState: reserved/locked items or backend escrow locations under one authoritative policy
Eligibility: same safe zone/range, alive, not blocked, binding permits trade
CommandReceipt and ResultRevisionA/B: durable final outcome
commands: UpdateTradeOffer(CommandId, TradeId, ExpectedOfferRevision, Items, Currency) -> Updated|StaleOffer|BoundItem
flow: A requests trade with B; backend validates both authenticated sessions, same-zone safe/range policy and blocks, then creates one trade record.
Each offer update references exact items/currency. Reserve them under a declared backend escrow/lock policy so they cannot also be sold/crafted/equipped.
Changing either offer increments revision and clears both acceptances; UI displays the revised item details/quantities prominently.
Both accept the same revision. Backend locks both characters and escrow rows in sorted CharacterId order, rechecks binding/ownership/capacity/currency and active sessions.
One transaction exchanges all items/currency, releases escrow, stores receipt and updates both revisions. A gear UUID moves unchanged.

Disconnect/cancel before commit returns escrow atomically; after commit, cancellation returns AlreadyCommitted and both players reconcile the same final trade. Cross-zone transfer refuses while escrow is unresolved.
editor_steps: Create trade schema/contract and DA_TradePolicy_Default with safe-zone/range and item binding restrictions. Keep auction houses disabled.
Build WBP_Trade with two clearly labeled offer panels, offer revision, currency, item tooltips, acceptance indicator and explicit confirm/cancel.
Add URPGTradeComponent to authorized player/social route; inventory mutations consult escrow reservations.
Reopen merchant/craft/equipment/bank to reject reserved items consistently; reopen zone transfer to drain/cancel unresolved trade before departure.
Seed Sword_A and Ore_B, full-bag, blocked-pair, changed-offer and disconnect-after-commit fixtures.
failures: B changes offer after A accepts -> both acceptances cleared; no old-amount commit.
Same item offered in two trades or sold concurrently -> reservation/ownership check rejects one.
Destination lacks capacity -> no partial exchange; escrow remains editable or cancels under policy.
Disconnect after committed trade -> both durable results remain; no return of already-traded items.
Bound item/negative currency/overflow -> rejected before commit.
tuning: Initial direct trade only, same safe zone, four items per side and bounded currency. Escrow timeout proposal 120 seconds. Expand only after contention/recovery tests, not before economy operations are stable.
observability: Audit both participant IDs, offer revisions, acceptances, item UUID movement and receipt. Never obscure last-second offer changes; accessible confirmation is part of fraud prevention.

title: Factions, reputation and service unlocks
purpose: Simple authored factions give recorded standing gains/losses, thresholds and service/quest/price unlocks. Reputation changes come from validated events and should not make required progression permanently impossible.
fields: FactionId: stable faction.* ID
Standing: bounded integer, proposed -3000..12000
Thresholds: strictly increasing named tiers
ReputationEventId/source entitlement: deduplicated durable change
ServiceModifiers: authored price/unlock/quest conditions, versioned
RecoveryRoute: alternate quests/services for required progression
flow: Quest/world-event/combat policy emits a verified reputation entitlement with faction and bounded delta.
Backend deduplicates, clamps within allowed range, persists event/standing and returns new revision.
Zone updates owner reputation view and re-evaluates relevant NPC/dialogue/trainer/vendor conditions.
Merchant quote includes the current reputation modifier/version; a change invalidates stale quotes under the chosen quote policy.
UI explains standing thresholds and affected unlocks without recomputing authoritative prices.
Content validation ensures the main quest route has recovery/alternate access when optional faction choices reduce standing.
editor_steps: Author RiverCompact, CairnWardens, AshenSurvey and TideboundLeague faction definitions with original text and bounded tiers.
Create DA_Faction_RiverCompact and one +100 RoadSupplies reward event as a fixture.
Add URPGReputationComponent to PlayerState and WBP_Stats reputation view.
Reopen NPC/dialogue/quest/vendor/trainer definitions for explicit standing requirements and modifier IDs.
Add negative-standing and threshold-crossing fixtures, including reconnect and stale merchant quote.
failures: Replay reputation reward -> unchanged standing.
Client submits arbitrary delta -> InvalidSource.
Threshold table unsorted -> validation fails.
Required story service inaccessible after optional choice -> content gate fails until alternate route exists.
tuning: Proposed thresholds Neutral=0, Recognized=1000, Trusted=3000, Honored=6000; all tuning. No full faction war/geopolitical simulator.
observability: Audit source entitlement and before/after tier. Use text tier names and numeric progress; do not rely only on faction colors.

title: NPC training, recipe unlocks and profession gates
purpose: Trainers sell or grant validated ability/profession/recipe unlocks through a service catalog. They do not directly modify skill arrays in a widget or own duplicate progression records.
fields: TrainerId and OfferId: versioned authored catalog
UnlockKind: Ability|Recipe|Profession|RespecService
Requirements: class/level/reputation/profession/quest IDs
PriceBaseCurrency and QuoteExpiry: server-calculated
UnlockEntitlementId: unique character/offer or definition key
flow: Interact with Tovin and receive offers filtered by current character build and service permissions.
UI shows missing requirements and exact quote; confirmation sends only the quote/offer identity.
Backend validates range/session through trusted zone context, requirements, currency and existing entitlement.
Commit currency debit and unique unlock in one transaction; return updated profession/recipe/ability IDs.
Zone rebuilds appropriate GAS/crafting/profession view and UI marks Learned.
Respec delegates to the skill respec transaction, not an independent trainer-side point reset.
editor_steps: Author DA_Trainer_Tovin with Blacksmithing entry, IronHatchet recipe and class respec service.
Assign trainer service to NPC_Tovin without copying character progress into its Blueprint.
Use WBP_Skills/WBP_Crafting relevant panels or a trainer offer tab with read-only offer views and pending actions.
Reopen wallet/skill/craft components to consume committed unlock entitlements.
Test locked, already-known, insufficient funds and concurrent purchase cases.
failures: Purchase same unlock twice -> one debit/entitlement.
Quest/reputation requirement changes -> RequirementsFailed or refreshed quote.
Client requests unlisted ability -> InvalidOffer.
tuning: Trainer costs/levels are proposals. Initial class baseline abilities remain available without a paid trap that blocks required progression.
observability: Record offer/unlock/quote and receipt. Explain why an offer is locked in localized text.

title: Safe hubs, roads, boats and paid fast travel
purpose: Long-distance traversal uses authored roads/gates/boats and later unlocked safe-hub travel. Fast travel is a validated zone-transfer request with optional cost, not a client teleport to an arbitrary map coordinate.
fields: HubId/ZoneId/EntranceId: registered safe destination
UnlockedHubIds: durable discovery/quest entitlement
TravelQuoteId and Cost: bounded integer, versioned
TravelPaymentId: linked to TransferId and compensation policy
Eligibility: not in combat/dead/trading/gathering, source service context valid
flow: Player unlocks a safe hub through verified discovery/quest and sees it on the map.
At an authorized travel service, select another unlocked hub and receive a quote with destination/cost.
Backend reserves or escrows payment linked to a new TransferId while validating eligibility/capacity; do not charge repeatedly on every connection retry.
Use the same signed-ticket/session-fenced zone handoff as road gates. A boat can use this transfer with authored departure presentation, not real vehicle simulation initially.
Capture cost on the declared successful handoff milestone; definitive failed reservation/transfer triggers a once-only refund/escrow release. Unknown outcomes reconcile first.
On arrival spawn at registered safe entrance and clear old map/NPC contexts.
editor_steps: Author hub definitions for Hearthford and Kestrel shelter, with exact entrance IDs and unlock conditions.
Add map marker actions and travel NPC/boat interaction; route to URPGFastTravelComponent.
Extend backend transfer record with payment linkage/terminal compensation state.
Reopen zone transfer recovery to distinguish unknown from definitive failure before refunding.
Test full destination, expired ticket, payment response loss and arrival acknowledgement loss.
failures: Locked hub -> HubLocked, no reservation or charge.
Transfer succeeds but ack lost -> receipt reconciliation captures once; no free duplicate refund.
Reservation definitively fails -> no charge or one escrow release.
Client requests coordinates/map path -> InvalidDestination; only catalog IDs allowed.
tuning: First fast travel may be free for simpler proof, then add a modest fixed price. Roads remain meaningful; mounts and seamless world travel are separate systems.
observability: Trace travel payment and TransferId together. UI explains cost/refund/pending state and provides accessible destination list navigation.

title: Mount feasibility and later movement/content gate
purpose: Mounts are a later committed content system only after movement, camera, collision and animation feasibility pass. No mounted sprite, riding pose, mount creature or equipment compatibility is claimed to exist in the archive.
fields: MountDefinitionId and unlock entitlement: durable IDs
MountedMovementProfile: approved speed/collision/turn policy
MountedAppearanceSetId: body/mount/gear actions and facings, source-verified
DismountSafeTransform: server collision/navigation validated
Combat/Water/InteriorPolicy: initially dismount or reject; authored
flow: Production first proves a developer-authored placeholder mount in the terrain lab, not on a live economy server.
Server validates unlock, zone rules and current action state before changing the movement profile.
Presentation selects a complete mounted set for current facing/action; do not stretch a walking person onto an invented animal.
Dismount finds a valid capsule position and restores the ordinary movement profile once.
Death, transfer, interiors and water use explicit dismount policy; no mount state persists as stale Actor pointers.
Only after art/latency/navigation/camera tests pass may mount entitlements be enabled in catalogs.
editor_steps: Create a feasibility-only mount definition and record all missing sprite/mesh/action requirements. Keep its production Enabled flag false.
Add a test profile to L_TerrainLab with slopes, bridges, doorways and water shores.
Implement movement-profile switching through the existing movement component; no parallel mount teleport integrator.
Create/commission riding/mount art with common root and four/eight-facing plan, then fill appearance matrix and licenses.
Reopen zone/interior/fast-travel rules and UI to show Unavailable until the gate is approved.
failures: No mounted art -> ArtUnavailable; ordinary movement unaffected.
Dismount inside wall -> NoSafePosition or validated fallback, not clipping.
Mount speed intent forged -> server profile/correction wins.
Transfer while mounted -> documented dismount before snapshot; no duplicate body.
tuning: No production mount speed or unlock cost selected. This gate prevents premature movement/art work from blocking Slice A/B.
observability: Record feasibility results separately from shipped feature status. Mount action has remappable input and no mandatory rapid timing.

title: Guild membership, roles and durable social administration
purpose: Guilds provide durable membership, roles, invitations and guild chat after basic parties/economy operate safely. Initial guilds do not include a guild bank, territory simulation or monetization.
fields: GuildId UUID; NameNormalized; GuildRevision
Membership: one guild per character initially; unique membership record
Role: Member|Officer|Leader with explicit capability matrix
InviteId/Expiry and inviter capability
LeadershipTransferId: authenticated explicit operation, audit record
GuildChatPermission: membership/moderation/block policy
flow: Authenticated eligible character creates a unique named guild under moderated naming rules and receives leader role in one transaction.
Invitations verify officer capabilities and target block/membership constraints; acceptance creates one membership.
Every role/kick/disband/leadership mutation validates capability and revision on backend, not a visible UI button alone.
Zone/social projections publish guild tag/name and authorized member list; private account IDs remain hidden.
Guild chat reuses moderated chat routing; membership changes invalidate delivery rights promptly.
Disconnect/restart preserves roles and pending invitation policy. Leader departure requires explicit transfer/recovery rather than accidental orphaning.
editor_steps: Create guild schema and capability matrix, DA_GuildPolicy_Default and GuildFixture_Riverwatch.
Build WBP_Guild with roster, role labels, invites, leave and explicit leadership confirmation.
Reopen chat/nameplates/social service for guild-safe public metadata and channel permissions.
Add moderator recovery procedure for abandoned leadership with audit and appeal policy; do not create an unaudited admin override in client Blueprint.
Test role escalation, stale revision, last leader and duplicate name cases.
failures: Member forges officer role RPC -> Forbidden.
Two leadership changes race -> one valid revision result.
Leader leaves without successor -> LeaderTransferRequired.
Blocked/private data leaked via guild lookup -> security test failure.
tuning: Initial cap 30 members is a proposal, not a scalability result. Guild bank/housing/raids remain separate optional expansions with additional economy/operations gates.
observability: Audit role/membership changes and moderator interventions. Guild UI supports list navigation, text scaling and clear destructive-action confirmations.

title: World events, ambient villagers and later schedules
purpose: Small server-owned zone events create shared activity without requiring an ecosystem simulator. Ambient villagers/fishers can animate locally; schedules that change service availability require authoritative time and recovery rules.
fields: WorldEventId and CycleId: unique reward namespace
Start/EndServerTime, phase and revision
ParticipationEntitlements: verified character actions, not simply UI presence
EventSpawn/ResourceModifiers: bounded authored changes
NPCScheduleId and TimeBuckets: optional later content; service fallback location
RewardClaimId: unique character/event/cycle key
commands: ApplyNPCSchedule(TimeBucket) -> DestinationRoleState|Blocked; server for meaningful movement/services
flow: Server time/controller selects a permitted event cycle and records start/end/phase.
Event spawns bounded encounters or requests deliveries through existing systems; it does not implement separate loot/inventory rules.
Verified participation events create eligibility; completion grants rewards once per cycle through the common transaction service.
Clients receive phase/timer/marker cues and ambient effects. Late joiners see current state, not a history of reward notifications.
On restart resume/cancel the recorded cycle under policy without creating a new reward cycle implicitly.
Later NPC schedules move via navigation to authored locations; critical services keep a fallback contact/location so day/night does not strand progression.
editor_steps: Author Riverwatch event: defend the road warning post and deliver repair supplies. Reuse encounter/quest/item definitions with event-cycle context.
Place BP_WorldEventController and NPC_AmbientFisher, a nonrewarding ambient visual actor unless explicitly promoted to a service.
Bind notification/map/quest UI to event phase and server time.
Create schedule table with Day/Night location IDs only after path/door/streaming tests; keep scheduling disabled in the first implementation.
