Test overlapping event/resource quotas and restart at resolving phase.
failures: Replay participation/reward -> one count/grant.
Server restarts -> same cycle or explicit canceled result, not a fresh farmable reward.
Scheduled NPC path blocked -> fallback service remains accessible; no teleport through players/geometry.
Ambient animation notify -> no fish/items spawned into economy.
tuning: One small event per initial zone and 15-minute active duration are proposals. Full ecological/geopolitical simulation is out of scope.
observability: Log cycle/phase/participation and spawn quotas. Event objectives have readable text and clear opt-in context; no mandatory audio-only alarms.

title: Audio, particles and 2D/3D presentation cues
purpose: Make accepted actions readable without allowing particles, sprite frames or sounds to grant damage, resources or loot. A missed cue may look wrong but must never leave gameplay stuck.
fields: CueId: stable cosmetic catalog key
ActionId and ServerStartTime: visual correlation, not reward credentials
AttachmentAnchor: Feet|HandMain|HandOff|WorldPoint; offsets per facing
SoundVolume: local 0..1 master/music/effects/voice sliders
ReducedFlash and MotionReduction: local accessibility flags
MaxConcurrentCues: per client budget; suppress lowest priority first
commands: PlayLocalCue(CueId, ActionId, Anchor) -> CueHandle|MissingCue; cosmetic custom API
flow: Input may start an inexpensive predicted swing cue with its local action correlation.
Server accepts or rejects the action using combat/gathering rules independently of the cue.
Accepted presentation state includes action identity, target/world point and start time; remote clients resolve the authored cue.
The cue adapter samples the current facing anchor, spawns world-space projectile/impact particles or plays sound, and avoids triggering twice when prediction is confirmed.
Rejected action fades/cancels the predicted cue; late remote presentation catches up within a bounded visual window.
Destroy or pool visual components on completion, possession change and zone unload; no cue callback calls a reward or health setter.
editor_steps: Create DA_CueSet_Common with mappings for Cleave, ArrowImpact, OreHit, WoodHit, FishBite, CraftComplete and LevelUp; rights-cleared sound/VFX assignments remain explicit authoring tasks.

Create Niagara systems only after checking the installed Niagara tooling; use engine primitive debug circles and text markers until assets exist. Do not treat a particle collision event as a server hit.
Attach URPGPresentationCueComponent to the player/enemy presentation root; define foot and hand offsets in DA_AnimationSet_Common per facing/page.
Bind audio sliders in WBP_Options to local audio settings, not replicated attributes. Include mute, subtitle/visual cue toggles and reduced-flash controls.
Place CueEmitter_A in L_ArtLab and trigger each cue from the diagnostics adapter with no gameplay state changes; repeat during a two-client combat run.
failures: Missing cue asset -> one rate-limited MissingCue warning; gameplay still completes.
Late confirm for canceled action -> no second sound/particle and no gameplay grant.
Zone unload while particle alive -> destroy/pool safely, no stale Actor dereference.
Muted audio -> fishing bite still has a readable visual timer.
Packet loss drops cosmetic cue -> health/loot state remains correct through replicated snapshots.
tuning: Proposed 32 nearby important cues and 16 ambient looping voices per client are profiling hypotheses, not measured budgets. Disable costly shadowed translucent particles on low settings.
observability: Log missing cue IDs once per catalog version, pooled component counts and rendering/audio cost. Never encode critical telegraphs only in sound or color.

title: Authentication boundaries, abuse prevention and privacy
fixture: L_NetworkLab / forged-client test harness / isolated backend fixture
purpose: Treat every network request as untrusted input. Authenticate identity at admission, validate ownership at every command and fence stale server sessions before they can write durable state. Security is a continuing process, not a claim that a dedicated server prevents cheating.
fields: AccountId/CharacterId: from validated identity mapping, never a trusted payload claim
SessionEpoch and LeaseOwner: backend-issued fencing values
CommandId/RequestHash: replay key with payload binding
RateLimitBuckets: action family, character/account and IP defense-in-depth
AllowedProtocol/CatalogVersions: exact compatibility set
AuditRetentionDays: documented policy requiring jurisdictional review; no invented compliance certification
flow: Backend verifies provider issuer/audience/signature/expiry/nonce and resolves a stable account identity. EOS is an optional provider interface, not the character database.
Zone verifies a one-use admission ticket bound to account, character, destination and protocol; do not pass bearer credentials through ordinary logged command-line URLs.
Each command checks current actor ownership, live state/range/rate and payload bounds; durable writes additionally require the current epoch and expected revision.
Backend uses parameterized SQL, narrow service credentials and server-side catalog validation; reject negative quantities, arithmetic overflow and unknown item IDs.

Rate-limited/rejected requests return stable reason codes, not secret details. Repeated impossible actions produce auditable signals for review rather than automatic punishment based on one lag spike.

Operational staff can revoke sessions and investigate ledger/command IDs under least privilege; logs exclude passwords, tokens, private message contents unless retention policy explicitly permits protected moderation evidence.
editor_steps: Configure development authentication only for loopback/private environments and make production service startup fail when the fixture provider is selected.
Create two service credentials: zone mutation/admission capability and administrative migration/backup capability; never package either in client assets.
Reopen BP_ZoneGameMode admission path so unauthorized connections cannot possess a pawn before validation completes.
Add request-size/count limits and per-command cooldown/rate checks in native handlers; expose diagnostics counters read-only to WBP_Diagnostics in development builds.
Create malicious request fixtures for other-character IDs, stale epochs, duplicate command IDs with changed payloads, oversized chat and negative quantities.

Write privacy, deletion, retention and support-contact policies for the actual deployment jurisdiction before public accounts; obtain appropriate review rather than claiming this manual is legal advice.
failures: Old zone sends inventory mutation after handoff -> StaleSession with zero rows changed.
Forged AccountId or item GUID -> Forbidden; no data disclosure.
Same command ID with changed amount -> IdempotencyConflict; do not return a receipt for a different payload.
Fast movement under high latency -> inspect movement correction history and approved modes before sanctions.
SQL metacharacters in name -> treated as data and validated; no SQL execution.
Leaked/rotated zone credential -> revoke and renew service identity; do not require rebuilding all clients.
tuning: Propose a 10 requests/second economic-command ceiling with a small burst allowance in the development fixture, then tune from real interaction patterns. Network movement uses engine cadence, not that economic limiter.
observability: Correlate account pseudonymous ID, character, epoch, command, outcome, latency and abuse rule. Publish retention boundaries and support escalation; no credentials in screenshots or crash reports.

title: Deployment, zone allocation and operational recovery
fixture: L_LoadTest / Zone_A and Zone_B / backend staging database
purpose: Operate a small persistent multi-zone game with measured capacities, reproducible builds, backups and a safe maintenance procedure. A dedicated UE process is a zone simulator, not a complete hosting or matchmaking platform.
fields: ZoneProcessId, BuildId, CatalogHash, RegionId: immutable registration metadata
HeartbeatSequence/LastSeen: monotonic liveness record
Capacity/Reservations/ActiveSessions: allocator counters, not a promised concurrency level
DrainDeadline: server-controlled UTC timestamp
BackupId/SchemaVersion/RestoreTestId: operational evidence
ServerTick/CPU/Memory/NetworkUsage: measured telemetry with timestamp
commands: RestoreStagingBackup(BackupId) -> VerificationReport; operator procedure, not a game RPC
flow: Build a versioned client and dedicated-server package from the same pinned engine/plugin/content revision; keep symbols and server logs privately.
Start PostgreSQL and one authenticated backend, apply checked migrations, then start two zone processes with separate IDs/ports and service credentials supplied outside content.
Each zone registers its zone/catalog/build and begins admitting players only after definitions, persistence adapter and safe spawns are ready.
Allocator chooses a compatible zone with reserved capacity; it must count in-flight reservations to avoid overfilling.
On maintenance, stop new admissions/economic starts, settle commands, snapshot/fence sessions and offer safe reconnect/transfer. Terminate only after the drain policy or explicit failure handling.
Backups include database and required server configuration metadata; restore to an isolated environment and reconcile ledger/inventory/quest/session invariants before declaring the backup usable.
editor_steps: Document local ports explicitly: proposal backend HTTPS 7443, Zone_A game 7777 and Zone_B game 7787; firewall only required client game/admission paths. Validate actual packaged network configuration on the chosen platform.
Create DA_Deployment_Development containing nonsecret region/build/capacity settings. Keep all connection secrets in deployment secret storage or protected environment injection.
Launch the packaged dedicated-server executable using its actual generated name and map argument from the build; record the command from that build rather than copying an imaginary executable.
Open L_LoadTest with the same relevant actor populations as Rillmere: players, AI, nodes, projectiles and widgets on clients. A bare empty map is not a capacity proof.
Prepare runbooks for backend outage, database restore, zone crash, network partition, credential rotation, rollback and maintenance cancellation.
Run restore tests against disposable staging identities and check total balances, item uniqueness, reward receipts, session fences and content compatibility before permitting login.
failures: Heartbeat lost -> allocator stops new reservations; existing session authority is determined by lease/fencing, not heartbeat alone.
Zone full -> ZoneFull with retry/alternate compatible destination; do not disconnect source before a valid handoff plan.
Database unavailable -> economic actions reject/pend safely; no client-local fallback save.
Restore older database -> invalidate old tickets/epochs and reconcile acknowledged operations against recovery policy; never silently replay client receipts as grants.
Bad patch -> drain, restore compatible binaries/catalog and use a supported schema rollback/forward-fix; no untested down migration in production.
tuning: Begin with two to eight real clients and then measured 16/32-client tests. Proposed initial zone capacity 16 is a configuration ceiling for testing, not evidence it performs acceptably. Regional deployment starts with one region.
observability: Track admission failure, heartbeat age, reservations, save latency, command retry, database pool saturation, tick time and p95/p99 packet rates. Alert on sustained service health and invariants, not every transient timeout.

title: Replication, interest management and measured scale
purpose: Send each client only relevant state while preserving gameplay correctness. Begin with generic Actor replication, then measure before choosing Iris or Replication Graph; do not enable both.
fields: RelevantRadiusCm: per actor-family proposal, not visibility authority
NetUpdateFrequency/Dormancy: engine settings verified against installed version before use
PresentationSnapshot: action/facing/start-time/equipment IDs only
OwnerOnlyFacts: inventory/currency/quests/private state
NetworkProfile: latency, jitter, loss and bandwidth limits recorded per test
BenchmarkRecord: build/content/hardware/clientcount/duration/p95 metrics
commands: CollectNetworkSample(ActorFamily, Bytes, Relevancy) -> Metric; development instrumentation
CompareReplicationCandidate(BaselineRunId, CandidateRunId) -> ReviewRecord; test procedure, not game API
flow: Separate public world facts, owner-only character facts and cosmetic cues before choosing replication settings.
Generic replication sends movement and approved properties/RPCs; client sprite playback resolves compact state instead of replicating every sprite frame.
Resource actors become dormant when stable and explicitly wake on claim/depletion changes; late relevant clients receive the correct state, not only a past multicast event.
Measure actor/channel counts, bytes, RPCs, server tick and client render cost with representative AI/loot/projectiles; control the same scene and population for comparisons.
Profile generic baseline first. Select either Iris or Replication Graph in an isolated branch only when installed support and actual measurements justify migration.
Retest owner privacy, late join, dormancy wake, loss and zone handoff after every optimization. Never hide a valid combat target on the server because a client did not render it.
editor_steps: Add read-only counters to WBP_Diagnostics for net role, ping, current zone/epoch, relevant actor counts and received revision.
Set owner-only replication on private character projections; inspect remote clients for inventory/currency leaks.
Configure development network emulation using the installed engine network emulation settings/console help; record actual commands and verify whether latency applies per direction.
Run the same route at no impairment, 100ms RTT, 200ms RTT with jitter, and 2% loss; the exact emulation knob syntax is an installed-engine verification task.
Record captures from server plus two geographically separate or separately hosted clients, not only multi-PIE windows in one process.
Do not change Actor tick, update frequency and relevancy all at once; change one controlled variable and compare regression outcomes.
failures: Resource wakes from dormancy -> all newly relevant clients see depletion and cannot claim a stale generation.
Loss of cosmetic event -> later state converges without repeating rewards.
High latency inventory click -> pending state persists; no optimistic currency authority.
Remote player disappears outside interest radius -> quest/reward credit uses server policy, not visual presence.
Iris and Replication Graph both configured -> configuration validation fails before a performance comparison.
tuning: Initial diagnostic hypotheses: 30Hz dedicated simulation target, 16 players/zone, 100 active AI and 40 active resources in a test scene. These are load inputs, not achieved capacities. Establish acceptable p95 tick and bandwidth from target hardware and provider limits.
observability: Retain reproducible build/hardware/input/load records, raw captures and measured percentile summaries. Report the largest tested population and bottleneck; do not extrapolate to thousands without evidence.

title: Diagnostics, economy telemetry and support evidence
purpose: Make failures explainable without turning logging into another mutable gameplay database. Economic ledgers provide durable accounting; operational metrics explain latency, rejection and content balance.
fields: CorrelationId and CommandId: shared across client request, zone handler and backend receipt
EventName/SchemaVersion: stable allowlisted telemetry keys
OutcomeCode/DurationMs/RetryCount: numeric or controlled vocabulary
SourceSinkCurrencyDelta and ItemDefinitionId: accounting classifications; ledger remains canonical
PrivacyClass: Operational|Economic|ModerationRestricted
SamplingRate: 0..1 for high-volume noncritical metrics; no sampling of required ledger receipts
commands: RecordCommandOutcome(Context, ResultCode, DurationMs) -> Queued|SinkUnavailable; nonblocking metrics
flow: Attach one correlation ID when an interaction begins and propagate it through the owned RPC and backend command.
Commit the economic receipt and audit delta in the durable transaction; telemetry emission occurs after commit and can retry through the documented outbox without regranting.
UI shows Pending, Accepted or a friendly localized reason; diagnostics show the stable command ID for support.
Dashboards aggregate currency sources/sinks, item generation/destruction, rejection rates, gather yields and merchant stock pressure.
A metric sink outage does not block a valid committed transaction; required audit persistence failure does block a transaction whose policy requires it.
Support exports remove access tokens, private chat and machine secrets and identify build/catalog version before user approval.
editor_steps: Author a controlled error catalog in DA_TelemetryPolicy_Default and map codes to localization keys rather than exposing backend stack traces.
Reopen merchant, gathering, fishing and crafting handlers to record the same command/receipt IDs in their result events.
Build WBP_Diagnostics as a development-only screen with read-only epoch/revision/command state; never add buttons that directly set currency on production clients.
Create a synthetic purchase sequence from 1000 to 950 currency, a sell/buyback and a failed full-bag craft. Compare ledger changes to dashboard events.
Document retention/access and a minimal support report format: build, zone, approximate time, command ID, observed and expected behavior.
failures: Metric sink down -> transaction receipt still durable, UI confirms from authority.
Duplicate receipt delivery -> dashboard de-duplicates by receipt/event ID; no second economic grant.
Unknown error code -> generic safe message plus correlation ID, not a credential-containing exception.
Support bundle review -> tokens and service credentials absent.
tuning: Development logs may retain detailed command metadata; production sampling/retention are deployment decisions. No commercial analytics service is required to start.
observability: Use structured event keys and bounded labels; never label a metric with arbitrary player chat or unbounded item instance UUIDs. Audit access to sensitive records.

title: Content versions, schema migrations and patch compatibility
fixture: L_NetworkLab / schema-v1 and schema-v2 disposable databases
purpose: Keep saved identities stable across renamed assets, new content and software patches. Never interpret an unknown saved item/class/quest as permission to delete player progress.
fields: ProtocolVersion: network message schema compatibility
CatalogHash/DefinitionRevision: immutable released content identity
DatabaseSchemaVersion and MigrationId: ordered applied migration record
SaveRecordVersion: per serialized model shape
DefinitionRedirects: old ID -> new ID with reviewed migration reason
MinimumClientBuild: backend-enforced compatibility gate
flow: Assign stable semantic definition IDs independent of Content Browser file names and never recycle an old ID for a different item.
Author a migration with preconditions, data transformation, uniqueness checks, estimated lock/downtime and forward-recovery plan. Test on a restored staging copy.
Backend records each migration transaction/version and rejects incompatible servers until the catalog/schema set is supported.

At login/transfer, validate protocol, content and record versions before possession. Resolve reviewed redirects; quarantine unknown/inconsistent records for repair instead of granting default replacements repeatedly.
Deploy backward-compatible expand changes first, update services/servers/clients, migrate data, and contract old columns only after rollback window ends.
Patch acceptance replays old quest/inventory/skill/fishing receipts and verifies no duplicate reward, changed GUID or lost currency.
editor_steps: Create DA_ContentVersion_Development with ProtocolVersion=1 and an explicitly generated catalog manifest hash; do not use a hand-entered hash disconnected from cooked content.
Add version checks to login, zone reservation, transfer redemption and persisted snapshot decode.
Write numbered migration specifications under Backend/GameService/Migrations in the implementation repository; this manual provides contracts, not runnable backend code.
Create fixture records with an old item ID, unknown recipe, obsolete skill node and already-completed quest reward.
Run migration twice on disposable database copies; second application reports AlreadyApplied with unchanged counts.
Reopen WBP_Loading to display PatchRequired or RecoveryRequired and avoid endless reconnect loops.
failures: Unknown item ID -> quarantine/report while retaining owned record; no silent deletion or repeated compensation.
Migration interrupted before commit -> old schema/data remain or resumable explicit migration state; rerun does not double-transform.
Client catalog newer/older unsupported -> PatchRequired before live zone admission.
Redirect cycle -> content validation fails.
Restore backup from older schema -> apply tested forward migrations in isolation before live admissions.
tuning: Use one released catalog version per compatible deployment initially. Supporting multiple simultaneous catalogs is a later operational feature, not a default requirement.
observability: Log schema/catalog/protocol versions with migration and repair IDs. Keep a human-readable release manifest and restore evidence; exclude personally identifying rows from public examples.

title: End-to-end testing, packaging and release acceptance
fixture: L_Rillmere / L_Thornweald / L_SluiceVault / separate packaged clients
purpose: Prove the integrated player journey in a real packaged client/server environment, while distinguishing documentation static checks from gameplay verification. Release only the measured, tested scope.
fields: TestCaseId/BuildId/CatalogHash: reproducible identity
ClientCount/ServerCount/Hardware/Region: environment record
ExpectedOutcome/ObservedOutcome: separate fields
EvidencePaths: logs, captures and database assertions from actual execution
AccessibilityMatrix: keyboard/controller/text-scale/color/motion cases
ReleaseBlockers: unresolved defects with owner and severity
commands: RunAcceptanceCase(TestCaseId, FixtureProfile) -> TestRecord; future implementation test contract
AssertLedgerInvariant(CharacterId, ExpectedRevision) -> Pass|Violation; backend test adapter
flow: Build development and shipping client/server targets using the installed engine packaging route and actual supported platform toolchain.
Deploy an isolated backend/database and two zone processes from the same release manifest; provision two or more real test accounts.
Execute Slice A, then Slice B, then the online-ready route with party/dungeon/social flows and documented fault injection.
For every economic action, compare UI, authoritative state, database rows and command receipt after retry/disconnect/zone change.
Run navigation/accessibility/localization/layout tests with long text, keyboard-only and controller focus; verify opening menus does not pause the server.
